# 2.0.0: API cleanup, the announced removals, three feature gaps and 128-bit tiers

## Purpose

The core split shipped as `2.0.0-preview.2` with three packages, new namespaces and a new repository name, and by plan left the API's shape unchanged: the split plan called the renames "a separate workstream that lands in the same major after this plan". This document is that workstream, plus the three feature gaps that the 2026-09-04 reference-library evaluation found worth closing before the major closes. It also gives 128-bit tiers to the kernels that run scalar on a default NativeAOT publish and on WebAssembly.

It sets what changes, in which order, and why. Each piece is verified under the mandatory test-first workflow. When the plan completes, its durable content moves into [specs/qrcode-symbologies.md](../specs/qrcode-symbologies.md) and the per-symbology records, and this file is deleted.

A public API is added in a minor and removed only in a major. 2.0.0 is the only release that can correct the accumulated naming drift, the value-type inconsistencies and the deprecated overloads at once, and consumers already edit every `using` line for the namespace change. Two edits in one line of caller code (`ECCLevel` → `QREccLevel` next to `CreateQrCode` → `Create`) cost the same as one. Phases 1-3 exist for that reason. After 2.0.0 the next chance is 3.0.0.

## Scope

| In | Out |
|---|---|
| The announced removals (`Compression`, `GetRequiredBufferSize` ×2, parameter-list generator overloads) | `CancellationToken` / time-budget decode overloads (additive, 2.1.0) |
| Type and method renames under one naming rule | Payload helpers (deferred by the maintainer and unchanged) |
| Value-kind, immutability and sealing unification | GS1 / FNC1 (unchanged) |
| Symbol geometry in the decode result | A pure-BCL SVG / 1-bit PNG writer (waits for a concrete request) |
| Structured Append, encode and decode (Standard QR only) | `EciMode` as a value type (decided against, see D7) |
| Kanji encoding for all three symbologies | Additional renderer packages |
| Migration table and a mechanical replacement script | Readability heuristics for styled output |
| 128-bit tiers where x64 without AVX or WebAssembly runs scalar | The instruction set a NativeAOT publish targets, and README guidance on it |
| | Decoder options on the decode overloads (decided against, see D8) |

Features are additive and could ship in 2.1.0 without breaking anyone. They are in 2.0.0 because the maintainer chose a feature-complete major over a rename-only one. Kanji encoding is the largest and last of them. It was placed last so it could move to 2.1.0 if it slipped, but on 2026-09-29 it was decided that Kanji encoding ships in 2.0.0 and does not move to 2.1.0. It changes the default output for Japanese text, which D5 accepts only in a major, so a slip delays 2.0.0 instead of demoting the phase.

The 128-bit tiers are internal and could ship in any 2.x. They are in 2.0.0 because the design treats NativeAOT and WebAssembly as first-class, and most users will first measure 2.0.0. Unlike Kanji, they move to 2.1.0 if they slip, because they change no output.

## The naming rule

One rule decides every name in both packages:

> A prefix names the symbology. No prefix means all three. The prefixes are `QR` (Standard QR), `MicroQR` and `RmQR`. A noun that denotes a code keeps the `{Sym}Code` form (`QRCodeData`, `MicroQRCodeGenerator`, `RmQRCodeDecodeInfo`). Everything else (enums, ranges, strategies) takes the short prefix. Three-letter acronyms are Pascal-cased (`Ecc`, `Eci`, `Bom`), as the existing `EccLevel` properties already are.

Micro QR and rMQR were built after the rule became implicit and already follow it. Every violation is in Standard QR, which was written first, or in a shared type that took the `QRCode` prefix while meaning "the family". The rule removes that double meaning of `QRCode` (Standard QR in `QRCodeData`, the family in `QRCodeDecodeStatus`).

### Core (`FeatherQR`)

| Now | 2.0.0 | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `ECCLevel` | `QREccLevel` | The only unprefixed enum. Siblings are `MicroQREccLevel` and `RmQREccLevel` |
| `QRCodeSegmentation` | `QRSegmentation` | Siblings are `MicroQRSegmentation`, `RmQRSegmentation` |
| `QRCodeVersionRange` | `QRVersionRange` | Sibling is `MicroQRVersionRange` |
| `QRCodeDecodeStatus` | `DecodeStatus` | Shared by all three symbologies. It moves out of `QRCodeDecodeInfo.cs` into its own file |
| `QRCodeGenerator.CreateQrCode` | `QRCodeGenerator.Create` | The class already names the symbology, which removes the `Qr` / `QR` casing question |
| `MicroQRCodeGenerator.CreateMicroQRCode` | `MicroQRCodeGenerator.Create` | Same |
| `RmQRCodeGenerator.CreateRmQRCode` | `RmQRCodeGenerator.Create` | Same |
| `QRCodeCalculatedSize.QrSize`, `MicroQRCodeCalculatedSize.QrSize` | `Size` | Matches `QRCodeData.Size`. rMQR's `Width`/`Height` stay |
| `QRCodeGeneratorOptions.Utf8BOM` | `Utf8Bom` | Acronym rule |
| `Internals.StandardQr`, `Internals.RmQr` (namespaces) | `Internals.StandardQR`, `Internals.RmQR` | Internal, same rule. The `Internals/RmQr` folder is renamed with the namespace, so folder and namespace agree as `MicroQR` and `StandardQR` already did |

### Rendering (`FeatherQR.SkiaSharp`)

| Now | 2.0.0 | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `QRCodeExtensions` | `SKCanvasExtensions` | It holds only `SKCanvas` extension methods. It is named after what it extends, as in the BCL |
| `QRCodeRenderer` | `SymbolRenderer` | Renders all three symbologies, so it takes no prefix. "Symbol" is the word both standards use |
| `QRCodeImageBuilderBase<TSelf>` | `SymbolImageBuilderBase<TSelf>` | Same reasoning, same word |
| `Vector2Slim` (public) | internal | Appears in no public signature. It is an implementation detail that leaked into the surface |

### Names that deliberately do not change

`QRCodeData`, `QRCodeGenerator`, `QRCodeDecoder`, `QRCodeGeneratorOptions`, `QRCodeCalculatedSize`, `QRCodeDecodeInfo`, `QRCodeImageBuilder`, `QRCodeImageDecoder` and their Micro/rMQR siblings are all "a code" nouns and keep their form. `EciMode`, `ModuleRect` and the shape classes are already correct.

## Removals

| Removed | Announced in | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `Compression` | 1.2.0 `[Obsolete]` | No API accepts or returns it |
| `QRCodeGenerator.GetRequiredBufferSize`, `MicroQRCodeGenerator.GetRequiredBufferSize` | 1.2.0 `[Obsolete]` | `TryGetRequiredBufferSize` is the whole sizing surface afterwards |
| Parameter-list `CreateQrCode` / `CreateMicroQRCode` overloads | Spec, "frozen, removed at 2.0.0" | rMQR never had them and is the shape the other two converge on |
| `QRCodeCalculatedSize` public constructor and `IsValid` | Not previously announced | Part of the value-kind unification below, not of the removals phase. `IsValid` duplicates the `bool` that `TryGetRequiredBufferSize` already returns |

`IconData()` is not on this list, although the approved API listing shows it as `[Obsolete]`. The type has a `required` member, and the compiler emits that marker on the implicit constructor to stop a pre-C#-11 consumer from bypassing the required-member check.

The phase handles two consequences:

- `SizingExceptionContractTest` disappears with its subject. It checks the frozen disagreement between the two deprecated sizing methods (`InvalidOperationException` vs `ArgumentException` for overflow, `ArgumentException` vs `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` for an undefined ECC level). With both throwing methods gone the disagreement is gone, and the spec paragraph describing it becomes a "lessons learned" entry instead of a live contract.
- The `options` parameter can be defaulted everywhere. The spec records the asymmetry "rMQR defaults it, the other two cannot, because their parameter-list overloads would make the call ambiguous", and the overloads removed here are its only cause. After the removal all three generators read `Create(text, ecc, in {Sym}CodeGeneratorOptions options = default)`, the shape the spec wanted and could not have.

## Shape unification

| Item | Now | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|---|
| `*CalculatedSize` | QR is a `record struct` with a public constructor, `init` setters and `IsValid`. Micro/rMQR are plain `readonly struct`s with internal constructors | One kind: `readonly struct`, internal constructor, get-only properties, no `IsValid`. It is an `out` parameter of a `Try` method, never something a caller builds |
| `*DecodeInfo` | Three `readonly struct`s with different member order. rMQR has no `MaskPattern` (correct, since rMQR has one fixed mask) | Same member order everywhere: `Status`, `Version`, `EccLevel`, `MaskPattern` where the symbology defines one, `ErrorsCorrected`, then the new geometry and Structured Append members |
| `GradientOptions` | `record class` holding `SKColor[]` and `float[]` through `init` properties, with a mutable `public static readonly Default` | `sealed class`, constructor copies both arrays, exposes them as read-only, structural equality over elements |
| `IconData` | `class` with public get/set properties and an `[Obsolete]` parameterless constructor | `sealed`, init-only properties, factory methods only |
| `QRCodeData`, `MicroQRCodeData`, `RmQRCodeData`, the three image builders | Non-sealed with no extension point | `sealed`. `SymbolImageBuilderBase<TSelf>` stays public and abstract with a `private protected` constructor. The shape classes stay open |

`GradientOptions` also has a live defect. A `record class` generates equality that compares `SKColor[]` by reference, so two gradients with identical colours compare unequal, and `GradientOptions.Default.Colors[0] = …` mutates the shared instance every caller uses. The same change fixes both, so it is in this phase instead of filed as a bug.

## `null` in the builder options (Phase 3b)

Two unrelated meanings of `null` share the fluent setters today, and only one is legitimate. Separating them closes F2, so F2 is absorbed here instead of shipping as the three additive setters it was filed as.

The first meaning is a redundant default. `WithColors(codeColor: null)` is black, `WithColors(backgroundColor: null)` is white, and `WithModuleShape(null)` is plain squares. Each of those states already has a public value that names it: `SKColors.Black`, `SKColors.White`, `RectangleModuleShape.Default`. `SymbolRenderer` collapses the null on arrival (`var shape = moduleShape ?? RectangleModuleShape.Default;`), and in the Playground `CreateModuleShape` ends `_ => null, // rectangle (default)`, where a comment says what the argument cannot. A second spelling of a named state adds nothing and costs the reader a lookup.

The second meaning is an absent option. `WithGradient(null)`, `WithIcon(null)` and a clear colour of `null` are not defaults. An omitted gradient draws nothing. No default gradient is selected. `GradientOptions.Default` is a default gradient, not the absence of one, so it is no argument against the null. A clear colour of `null` is the same kind of state: the padding follows the background, a rule and not a colour anyone could pass.

`WithFinderPatternShape(null)` was filed as a third state, and measurement put it in the first. `ResolveFinderShape` returns `null` only when the modules are unstyled and substitutes `RectangleFinderPatternShape.Default` when they are styled (the #399 protection), so `null` looked like auto rather than plain squares. Comparing the bitmaps of both spellings shows otherwise: omitting the shape and naming `RectangleFinderPatternShape.Default` differ in 0 bytes of 360,000, with plain modules and with a transparent background. Auto and the named square give the same raster output through two draw paths, so the null is a second spelling and the parameter becomes non-nullable with the rest. The builder keeps the fast path, and so the internal state, for callers who never ask for a shape. A caller who names the square gets the finder pass and the same pixels.

The review round found two errors in that first measurement. The third case it cited, circle modules at 0.85, proves nothing: `ResolveFinderShape` substitutes the square for any styled module set, so both spellings pass the same argument and only one path runs. And the equivalence holds only for raster. Where the two spellings take different paths (plain modules, where omitting means the merged-run path), the SVG documents differ, and where the background alpha is also below 255 the named square loses the finder patterns, because the finder pass cuts their light rings out with `SKBlendMode.Clear` inside a `SaveLayer` and `SKSvgCanvas` drops the layer. With styled modules the documents are identical, and both lack their finders. That defect predates this phase and belongs to the renderer. This phase owned the claim, which it stated per output kind in [qrcode-symbologies.md](../specs/qrcode-symbologies.md) and in the migration guide, together with the limitation. (F3 below fixed the limitation on 2026-09-13, and both documents now say pixels rather than elements, because the element counts still differ and always will.)

The rule, which generalises beyond these seven parameters:

> `null` means the option is absent, never "the default value". A default that has a name is passed by name.

| Setter | `null` today | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|---|
| `WithColors(codeColor, backgroundColor, clearColor)` | all three optional. Each omitted one is assigned its default | `WithColors(SKColor codeColor, SKColor backgroundColor)`, both required, and it sets only the two it names |
| (none) | (none) | new `WithCodeColor(SKColor)`, `WithBackgroundColor(SKColor)`, `WithClearColor(SKColor?)` |
| `WithModuleShape(ModuleShape?, float)` | plain squares | `ModuleShape`, non-null, `ArgumentNullException`. Pass `RectangleModuleShape.Default` for squares |
| `WithFinderPatternShape(FinderPatternShape?)` | auto, which renders as plain squares | `FinderPatternShape`, non-null, `ArgumentNullException`. Pass `RectangleFinderPatternShape.Default` for squares |
| `WithGradient(GradientOptions?)`, `WithIcon(IconData?)` | no gradient, no icon | unchanged. This is the legitimate null |
| clear colour | padding follows the background | unchanged meaning. Set with `WithClearColor`, and the state where none is set is the builder default, reachable again with `WithClearColor(null)` |

The rule fixes F2 without a patch. The reported defect is that `.WithColors(clearColor: Transparent)` appended to a chain resets the background to white. With colours non-nullable and no optional parameters on `WithColors`, the argument that "was omitted and got overwritten" cannot be written. The caller uses `WithClearColor` because nothing else compiles. This is the CodeGlyphX shape the F2 survey found (required-argument `WithColors` plus single-colour setters), reached from the nullability rule rather than copied.

The static surface keeps its nulls, mostly for a language reason. The `SKCanvas.Render` extensions take every option as an optional parameter, and so does `SymbolRenderer.Render` for the shapes, the gradient and the icon. A C# optional parameter needs a constant default: `ModuleShape moduleShape = RectangleModuleShape.Default` does not compile, and `SKColor codeColor = default` is transparent black, not black. There `null` is the only spelling of "argument not supplied", so it stays. The review round caught one exception: `SymbolRenderer.Render`'s `codeColor` and `backgroundColor` were required parameters typed `SKColor?` on all three overloads, so the optional-parameter reason did not apply to them. They were nullable for consistency with the extensions that forward to them, not for the language, and their XML docs said "Black when omitted" of a parameter that cannot be omitted. The docs are corrected here. The signatures were left for a separate decision outside this builder phase (decided and changed on 2026-09-13, F4 below). The builder has no such constraint, so the rule applies there in full.

The change keeps the output. The renderer already resolves `null` to the values the builder will now hold (`?? SKColors.Black`, `?? SKColors.White`, `?? RectangleModuleShape.Default`), so for the colours and the module shape only what a caller can express changes, and the golden-pixel tests guard the output. A caller's output can change only through the migration itself: rewriting `WithFinderPatternShape(null)` as `WithFinderPatternShape(RectangleFinderPatternShape.Default)` moves the finders onto the finder pass, which is pixel-identical in raster and dropped them from SVG over a non-opaque background until the 2026-09-13 fix (F3 below). Leaving the setter uncalled, which is what the `null` meant, changes nothing.

## Feature work

### Symbol geometry in the decode result

No reference library returns the symbol's position for Standard QR (CodeGlyphX does only for Micro QR), so this sets the library apart, and it is cheap: the corners are the image decoders' existing `PerspectiveTransform` applied to the four corners of module space.

Before writing it, D3 settles which four points, in which space, in which order, and what a matrix-level decode reports. The intended answer is the outer corners of the module area excluding the quiet zone, in source-image pixel coordinates, ordered from the symbol's own top-left so the quad also shows rotation and mirroring. A matrix-level decode leaves the member at its default, with a documented way to tell that apart. The type is a small `readonly struct` pair in the core. It does not use `System.Numerics.Vector2`, which on netstandard2.0 would add a package dependency to a package that advertises none.

### Structured Append (Standard QR only)

rMQR (recorded in [rmqr-encoder.md](../specs/rmqr-encoder.md)) and Micro QR do not define it and have no mode indicator for it, so no such stream can exist for them. For Standard QR the work has two sides:

- Decode rejected the mode as `UnsupportedContent` until Phase 5a (2026-09-15). It now reads the header, reports symbol index, total count and parity on `QRCodeDecodeInfo`, and returns that symbol's own text. A caller checks that the parity bytes agree and concatenates in index order.
- Encode splits content across symbols. The parity byte is the XOR of the whole input's bytes as the set writes them, in the set's one charset, taken once before splitting. A per-chunk computation can diverge from it when a chunk would have chosen another charset on its own. An encoder that writes Kanji segments XORs Shift_JIS bytes, so the same Japanese text correctly carries a different parity in a Kanji-mode set than in a UTF-8 one (the decode corpus holds both). QrCodeGenerator is a valid parity reference from 3.2.0 (`5c6fdfd`), but 3.1.0 writes 0.

Decided (D4, below) and shipped as one balanced method with no combine helper. The design, decisions and lessons are in the encoder and decoder records.

### Kanji encoding

All three symbologies decode Kanji mode today and none writes it. The scope row in [qrcode-symbologies.md](../specs/qrcode-symbologies.md) says "decode only, revisit on concrete demand". This phase flips that row. Its own plan settled which texts are written in Kanji mode and split the phase into 6.1-6.9. It was folded into the specs on 2026-10-02 (see the Phase 6 entry in the Progress log). The phase has four pieces:

1. A reverse table, Unicode → the 13-bit compacted value, generated by `tools/QRInteropFixtures` from the same sweep data that produced `ShiftJisKanjiTable`, so the two cannot disagree. Characters outside the JIS X 0208 repertoire have no reverse entry and fall through to Byte mode. That covers the CP932 readings of the seven divergent cells but not their JIS X 0208 readings, which would have an entry. The encoder leaves both out, so every cell it writes reads the same in both mappings.
2. A Kanji state in `ModeSegmenter` (7 states → 8) at a flat 13 bits per character, with per-symbology and per-version availability as `allowAlnum` / `allowByte` already have: Micro QR M3 and M4 only, all rMQR versions, all Standard QR versions. The per-symbology Kanji count-indicator tables already exist on the decode side.
3. `EncodingMode` gains Kanji. The enum excludes it today ("that enum names the modes the encoder can produce"). This phase makes that comment false.
4. Cross-verification against the external oracles (qrtool, ZXingCpp, ZXing.Net, libzint) plus committed fixtures, because a Kanji encoder that no third-party reader agrees with is worse than none.

The phase has two decisions. D5 asks whether single-mode selection picks Kanji automatically. Kanji is the cheapest single mode for Japanese text, so a yes changes the bytes the library emits by default for existing callers. That is acceptable in a major and is what other libraries do, but it must be a decision with a migration note, not a side effect. D6 asks whether a plan may mix Kanji segments with ECI-tagged Byte segments in one symbol. The standard allows it, and readers have historically handled it unevenly. The oracle sweep from piece 4 answers it, and the conservative fallback suppresses Kanji whenever an ECI header is emitted.

Decided (D5, D6, below) and shipped, with Kanji mode as an option, not the default. The rules, and why they are not wider, are in [qrcode-symbologies.md](../specs/qrcode-symbologies.md#when-kanji-mode-is-written).

## 128-bit tiers for builds without AVX2

Done on 2026-10-01, in 2.0.0. Every scalar cell in the x64-without-AVX and WebAssembly columns of `SimdTiers.Expected` was raised or kept with its measured reason, and the public API is unchanged. Its own plan was folded into [the 128-bit round](../specs/qrcode-symbologies.md#the-128-bit-round) (the rules a tier ships under, how each build is measured, the end-to-end result, the lessons) and the per-symbology records, then deleted.

## Open decisions

| # | Decision | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Drop the `string` convenience overloads once the parameter-list overloads are gone? | Decided 2026-09-06: drop all four (`QRCodeGenerator` ×2, `MicroQRCodeGenerator` ×1, `RmQRCodeGenerator` ×1). `string` converts implicitly to `ReadOnlySpan<char>`, so `Create("text", ecc)` keeps compiling and the overloads add only a parameter name. (The pre-PR review corrected this: it holds on three of the four assets, not all four. See the Phase 1-3 review entry in the Progress log.) `Create` becomes two methods per symbology, span and span-plus-destination, which also removes the asymmetry where only Standard QR had `(string, ecc, destination)` |
| D2 | `SymbolRenderer` / `SymbolImageBuilderBase<TSelf>` as the shared-renderer names | Decided 2026-09-06: adopt, together with `QRCodeExtensions` → `SKCanvasExtensions`. Both standards and these specs already call what all three symbologies produce a "symbol". The per-symbology `*ImageDecoder` / `*ImageBuilder` types keep their prefixes |
| D3 | Geometry contract: which corners, which space, which order, matrix-level behaviour | Decided 2026-09-07. The outer corners of the module area, quiet zone excluded, as `SymbolCorners` of four `ImagePoint`s (`float X`, `float Y`) in continuous image coordinates: (0, 0) is the top-left corner of the top-left pixel and (width, height) the bottom-right corner of the image, so the values plot directly in SkiaSharp / canvas / System.Drawing. The finder centres the decoders anchor on already use that convention, so nothing is shifted (the review round removed a +0.5 added on the opposite assumption). Ordered from the symbol's own top-left (the finder side) as `TopLeft, TopRight, BottomRight, BottomLeft`, so a mirrored capture shows reversed winding. Populated only when `Status == Success`. Matrix-level decodes and failures leave `Corners` at `default`, which `IsEmpty` reports. Both types are library-built `readonly record struct`s (internal constructor, get-only), per the Phase 3 rule |
| D4 | Structured Append encode API shape and whether a combine helper ships | Decided 2026-09-14, recorded in [standardqr-encoder.md](../specs/standardqr-encoder.md#structured-append) and [standardqr-decoder.md](../specs/standardqr-decoder.md#decisions). One method, `CreateStructuredAppend(text, ecc, options)`, whose symbol count follows the existing `options.Version` cap instead of a new parameter, because "fewest symbols" has no answer without a cap and the cap is what a caller has. Balanced so every symbol shares one version. A text that fits in one symbol returns one plain symbol with no header. No combine helper. The four reassembly rules are documented instead |
| D5 | Does `Segmentation.Single` choose Kanji mode automatically? | Decided 2026-10-01: no, only on request. It did during development, until a phone scan found that an Android phone's own scanners read no Kanji mode. `AllowKanji` (off by default) on all three options types turns it on, and an explicit `Utf8Bom` or `EciMode` keeps Byte mode with or without it |
| D6 | Kanji segments mixed with ECI-tagged Byte segments | Decided 2026-10-01: never. The sweep found zxing-cpp reads a Kanji segment after ECI 26 in the ECI's charset, as ISO/IEC 18004:2015 reads it, where ZXing and its ports read JIS X 0208. A text that would need both stays UTF-8 |
| D7 | `EciMode` enum → a value type with `FromValue` / `Value` | No. An encoder can emit only a charset it can convert text into (Latin-1 and UTF-8), and the decoder reports every other ECI as `UnsupportedContent` without carrying the number. A value type would also need a sentinel for "no ECI", which collides with the real ECI 0, only to express values nothing can produce or consume. Recorded as a scope decision with this reason instead of left open |
| D8 | Decoder options: an `in XxxDecoderOptions` parameter on the decode overloads before the Phase 7 freeze | Decided 2026-10-02: no. Raised by the decode pipeline review (2026-09-28, since folded into [qrcode-symbologies.md](../specs/qrcode-symbologies.md)): the generators take `in XxxGeneratorOptions` and the decoders take none, and a parameter added before the freeze would let a caller trade passes for speed without new overloads. Other readers' QR options fill no gap here. Inverted, mirrored and rotated symbols are always read, and cost extra only when the first reading fails. The decoder type chooses the symbology, and `Status` says why a decode failed. No caller has asked. The needs that could come later each want their own shape. A time budget or cancellation is a trailing `CancellationToken`, already scoped to 2.1.0, and a time limit works against Micro QR's attempt budget, which keeps a result independent of CPU speed. Faster failures for continuous camera scanning may want a reusable reader instead of a per-call struct. A switch that lifts the measured gates, such as rMQR's 6 px scale-search bound, fits a per-call struct. A charset for Byte segments with no ECI (11 corpus photographs carry Shift_JIS) is first a better guess, which needs no option. Several symbols per image need a new result type, not an option. Added later, options are new overloads beside the existing ones (the 12 image overloads, or all 24 if the option applies to matrix decodes), and a call without options still binds to the existing overload. Added now, the type would ship empty or with a field nobody asked for |

F3 to F7 came from the adversarial review of Phase 3b (2026-09-12). F8 and F9 came from the adversarial review of the renderer's colours (2026-09-13). F13 and F14 came from an exhaustive sweep of clean renders after those three landed, F15 from measuring F14, F16 and F17 from measuring F15, and F18 from a wider sweep of clean renders after F17 (all 2026-09-20). F20 to F23 came from the Structured Append work (2026-09-15 to 18) and moved here when its plan was folded (2026-09-29). F24 came from fixing F21 and F22 (2026-10-02). F1's renderer half was 2.0.0 work and landed on 2026-09-11. F2 also proved to be 2.0.0 work and became Phase 3b. Nothing left in this table blocks 2.0.0. Phase 7 folds this document into the specs and deletes it, so move this section somewhere that survives before then. A Progress log entry is history that nobody reads for work. This table is the list, so anything found and deferred belongs here as a row.

| # | Follow-up | Why it is not here | Shape |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | The square-symbology renderer fits its area (2.0.0). An axis-aware module size waits for a request. `SymbolRenderer.Render(canvas, area, …)` and the `SKCanvas.Render` extensions filled the given area for Standard QR and Micro QR, while rMQR's overloads and all three builders fitted. The same width and height gave a square-module symbol from a builder and a stretched one from the renderer, with no exception or warning, so the library had two geometry rules instead of one. | #400 was about what the builders produce. This is the renderer, a separate public surface with its own helpers and XML docs. The renderer half was still 2.0.0 work, because fitting is a breaking behaviour change, and it landed before the Phase 7 API freeze. The builder half that remains is not 2.0.0 work. | Renderer: decided and done 2026-09-11 (Progress log, "The low-level renderer fits its area"). Standard QR and Micro QR `Render` now do what rMQR's already did: background over the whole area, symbol at a uniform module scale centred in the letterboxed rectangle. The public `GetFinderPatternRect` and `GetIconRects` fit the same way in the same change. Otherwise they would return rectangles that disagree with the render for the same area (renders made while deciding this, not kept, showed outlines drawn from the caller's area landing beside the finders). Fitting a square into a square is the identity, so the helpers give the same answer for the caller's area or the fitted one, and square areas, the common case, render pixel-identically (measured at 512x512). Measured before and after with this library's decoder, a 900x450 canvas (Standard and Micro QR) and a 200x280 portrait slot with circle modules and an icon did not decode and now do. 512x480 decodes both ways and changes pixels, the class of change the migration guide already describes for `WithSize`. One difference stays: the builder snaps content to whole pixels because it owns the canvas, while the renderer uses the fit as computed because its area may sit under the caller's transform, so an odd leftover can shift edges by half a pixel. The rule is the same. The rounding differs. The same change dropped "the area is taken literally" from the `SymbolRenderer` and `SKCanvasExtensions` XML docs, rewrote the asymmetry paragraph in [qrcode-symbologies.md](../specs/qrcode-symbologies.md) as resolved, gave the renderer its own section in the migration guide, and moved `samples/Dotfiles/MigrationImages_1.x-2.0.cs` off the fill it used for its stretched "before" image. `WithModulePixelSize(x, y)` was decided on 2026-09-11 and deferred until a concrete request. Its one use case, an output device whose dot pitch differs by axis, was named during the #400 review as the reason to keep the fill. It appears in no issue, sample or report, and the public API growth rule allows no public API on anticipation. This row used to tie the two halves into one PR because "the second removes the only escape hatch the first replaces". That was assumed, not checked, and is false. Pre-distortion never needed a stretched area: `canvas.Scale(sx, sy)` over a square area reproduces the old fill exactly for plain modules and finders in a solid colour (0 differing pixels at 900x450, 600x400, 512x480 and 300x700), and a square area passes through the fit untouched, so the renderer change removes nothing a caller cannot still do in three lines. Styled output (shaped modules or finders, gradients, icons) is drawn in the square and stretched with it, so it can differ from what the old fill drew. Notes for whoever picks this up: the builder would have to apply the anisotropy as a canvas transform over square cells, because the renderer fits any non-square content rectangle it is handed to a square. A path that skipped the fit would still print `CircleModuleShape`'s dots squashed (old fill on a simulated 2:1 device: 4x8 px of ink in an 8x8 cell, against 8x8 with the transform) and the rounded shapes' corners uneven, because they size from the smaller side of the cell. Whether a pre-distorted bitmap decodes as a file depends on the reader (this library misses the 2:1 migration image, zxing-cpp reads it), so its docs would have to state up front that it is meant for the device, not a screen |

It is not: `WithColors`'s optional parameters read as "leave the rest alone" and behave as "reset the rest", and setters added beside them leave that reading in place. Removing the optional parameters is breaking, so it must happen before the Phase 7 freeze, not after 2.0.0. | The survey behind this row stands and is quoted in the Phase 3b section: no surveyed library offers an override-versus-merge choice. They remove the ambiguity. CodeGlyphX pairs a required-argument `WithColors(fg, bg)` with `WithForeground` / `WithBackground` / `WithTransparentBackground`. Spectre.Console has `Foreground()` / `Background()` on an immutable `Style` plus an explicit `Combine`. QRCoder takes colours as required positional arguments. ZXing keeps them off methods |

Found 2026-09-15 by the Structured Append fixture corpus: `codeglyphx/sixteen-symbols-max-v2-l-2of16`, a version 2-L symbol, mask 2, read from its PNG at 5 px/module and up. The locator finds all three real finders, each confirmed on every scanned row of its band, plus a fourth candidate at module (21.5, 18.5) in the bottom-right quadrant. That candidate is the alignment pattern's right ring plus two data modules: row 18 reads `1 0 111 0 1` from column 18, a clean 1:1:3:1:1. Column 21 reads 1:1:5:1:1 vertically, which the 50 % tolerance accepts, and the diagonal passes too. The selection took {top-left, top-right, false} over the real bottom-left for two reasons. The score was `spread / count`, which is zero for every triple on a render at a whole number of pixels per module, because all four candidates measure exactly the same module size. The count term was multiplied by zero and the tie went to the first window. And it scored only neighbours in module-size order, so with four equal sizes left in scan order (top-left, top-right, false, bottom-left) the correct triple was not among the two windows it scored. The ordering step then put the real top-right in the corner, because top-left to the false candidate was the longest side. The "15 modules" the first reading saw is real top-right to the false candidate. Version estimate, runner-up retry and format read all ran on that anchor. The confirmation filter sets the density boundary. The false pattern is one module tall, so at 3 and 4 px/module one scanned row hits it, it stays unconfirmed (count 1), and the `Count >= 2` compaction removes it. From 5 up it is confirmed and the tie decides | Found while landing Phase 5a, which is about the bit stream and does not touch the finder locator. The defect is in the three-of-many selection every Standard QR image decode uses, so it gets its own change and regression sweep | Done: selected by geometry. Every triple is scored by its distance from a right isosceles triangle (squared sides a ≤ b ≤ c, `(\|c − 2a\| + \|c − 2b\|) / c`, the same under rotation and mirroring) plus the relative module-size spread, with the confirmation count as the tie-break. Nothing new is rejected: any list that produced a triple before still produces one, and three candidates still return without scoring. On this symbol the correct triple scores 0.000 at every density from 3 to 16 px/module, and the three containing the false candidate score 0.333 to 0.393. A differential decode sweep of 20,000 renders from this library's encoder (flat, rotated, keystoned, both, and two symbols side by side) lost nothing and gained 364. The defect was not rare: 13 of the 40 flat failures were this class, and the old selector also mixed finders from two symbols whenever both were rendered at the same density (337 of 4,000). The fixture came off the known-defect list, which is gone with its guard. `FinderPatternSelectionTest` checks the selection and the image-level classes. Found by the F10 sweep, identical before and after that fix: flat, axis-aligned renders from this library's own encoder at versions 20 to 37 and 3 or 4 px/module (one case at 5) decoded a version one or two below the true one, 27 of 4,000 flat renders. The cause was that the module size was measured across the finder's two outer edges, which move apart when grey edge pixels fall on one side of the threshold. The sweep centres the symbol in a larger canvas, so its module edges land mid-pixel and come out grey. A grey just below the threshold widens every dark run by a pixel. The finder centres do not move (the distances were exact), but the 7-module span through the finder grew from 21 to 22 px at 3 px/module, +4.8 %, which is 4.8 modules over a version 24 span, past the snap and the runner-up retry. Smaller versions survived because their span is shorter. A lighter grey does the opposite and reads large symbols a version high | Pre-existing, found by the sweep that verified F10. The same branch fixed it | Done in four parts, because the unbiased module size exposed two alignment-search defects the bias had hidden. Module size comes from same-polarity edges: the dark ring's inner edge on one side and its outer edge on the other are 6 modules apart whatever the bloom, twice per line (12 modules in total), where the outer-to-outer span carried both edges' shift. The image path now reads version information: both 18-bit copies, from the matrix sampled at the estimated dimension (up to 3 errors corrected). They sit within 7 modules of a finder, so a dimension several modules off still samples them, and when they name another version that dimension is tried before the runner-up. Near-axis rotation at 3 px/module still quantizes the estimate up to 9 modules off, and the version information reads those. The alignment search returned the first hit in scan order, not the nearest to the prediction, so a false one to its left won while the real pattern sat on the prediction. It compared each run with the plain module size, although a row crosses a module rotated 45° √2 times longer, and each single run gains or loses the bloom pixel. It now keeps the hit nearest the prediction and re-centres it on its own row, derives the expected run per scan direction from the grid axes, checks light+dark pairs (same-polarity again) instead of single runs, and requires the light ring at ±1 module as well as the dark ring at ±2. In finder selection, F10's tie tolerance (1e-3) was sized on exact renders. Under keystone a false candidate at the fourth corner scored 0.016 better than the real triple while confirmed on less than a third of the rows, so the tolerance is now 0.05, applied in a second pass over the best score so ties cannot chain. The same work found the version clamp: an estimate a little past 177 modules rounded to version 41 and was refused as `NotDetected` |

The fit gives the symbol's corner and pitch per axis, and the dark runs give the size, on which both lines must agree. A line is read only if it looks like a timing pattern (runs 0.4-1.6 modules, size 11-17, pitch within 0.7-1.4 of the finder's). ## Phases

Each phase follows the test-first workflow, regenerates both `PublicAPI.approved.txt` files, updates `docs/migration.md` and the affected specs in the same change, and appends a Progress log entry with Done / Lessons / benchmark delta. A phase that moves a hot path measures it. A rename-only phase says it moved none.

| # | Phase | Contents | Exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Announced removals | The removals table. Retire `SizingExceptionContractTest`. Default the `options` parameter on all three generators | Surface shrinks, no rename yet |
| 2 | Renames | Both rename tables and the `string` overload removal from D1. Internal namespaces and test namespaces follow | One reviewable `PublicAPI.approved.txt` diff |
| 3 | Shape unification | `*CalculatedSize`, `*DecodeInfo` member set, `GradientOptions`, `IconData`, sealing (`Vector2Slim` went with the Phase 2 rename table) | API-final for the cleanup. Tag `2.0.0-preview.3` |
| 3b | Option nullability and colour setters | The `null` rule above: non-nullable colours and `WithModuleShape`, required-argument `WithColors`, the three single-colour setters (absorbs F2), corrected docs for the nulls that stay | Reopens Phase 3's API-final point. Golden pixels unchanged |
| 4 | Symbol geometry | D3, the geometry members on all three `*DecodeInfo`, all three image decode paths | Matrix-level decode behaviour documented and tested |
| 5 | Structured Append | D4, decode-side header reporting, encode-side split, parity over the whole input's bytes as the set writes them | Round-trip plus oracle cross-check |
| 6 | Kanji encoding | D5, D6, reverse table, segmenter state, `EncodingMode`, capacity docs. Sub-phases 6.1-6.9, done (see the Progress log) | Oracle sweep green. Tag `2.0.0-preview.4` |
| 6b | 128-bit tiers | Done 2026-10-01: [the 128-bit round](../specs/qrcode-symbologies.md#the-128-bit-round) | That plan's exit: every scalar cell in the x64-without-AVX and WebAssembly columns of `SimdTiers.Expected` raised or carrying its measured reason. Public API unchanged |
| 7 | Docs and API freeze | `docs/migration.md` 2.0.0 section rewritten with the full rename table and a mechanical replacement script. README, DESIGN.md, spec scope rows (Kanji, Structured Append, geometry, 128-bit tiers). Fold this plan into the specs and delete it, moving the Follow-ups table somewhere durable first (what remains there is not 2.0.0 work, so it cannot be folded in as history, and F1's renderer half landed and is already in the specs) | Approved API listing frozen |
| 8 | Release | Below | `2.0.0` on nuget.org |

Phases 4-6 are independent of each other and depend only on 1-3. Phase 6 is last and ships in 2.0.0 whatever it takes (decided 2026-09-29, see Scope), so Phase 8 waits for it. Phase 6b touches no public API, so it can run beside 4-6 or after the freeze. It must land before Phase 8 to be in 2.0.0 and moves to 2.1.0 if it slips. Phase 3b was found after Phase 4 shipped and runs in that order. It belongs to the cleanup, so it is numbered with it instead of appended, and Phase 3's "API-final" line held for the types it named but not for the builder's option signatures.

## Release checklist (Phase 8)

- `tools/QRInteropFixtures` manual spot-checks, each compared with its last result (a different result is a finding to explain before the release, and the fixture spec's oracle matrix has the detail):
  - `spot-check-kanji`: "every reader agrees with the input". Every encoder cell, in Standard QR (18 symbols, read by this library, zxing-cpp, ZXing.Net and CodeGlyphX), Micro QR (917) and rMQR (200, both read by this library and zxing-cpp). ASCII `\` and `~` in Kanji plans read as themselves in all three. Its ECI 26 table is not asserted: zxing-cpp 0.5.2 misreads a Kanji segment after ECI 26 (2026-10-01), which this library does not write.
  - `spot-check-structured-append`: 275 symbols read by three readers, 30 parity comparisons, 0 mismatches. The Japanese case is the UTF-8 set (parity 6) by default and a Kanji set with parity 176 under `kanji-opt` (`AllowKanji`, `Optimal`).
  - `spot-check-rmqr`: 444 of 444. `spot-check-microqr`: 18 of 18.
- Physical scanner acceptance pass, weighted toward Kanji-mode and Structured Append symbols, the two outputs no committed fixture can prove a phone accepts. The Kanji symbols, each written by this library with `AllowKanji`:
  - Standard QR:
    - 「こんにちは世界」 (one Kanji segment, 1-M)
    - 700 characters of Japanese at M (version 27 or above, a 12-bit count)
    - 「価格は\100~200円です、日本語のテキスト」 under `Optimal` (a Kanji plan, `\` and `~` in Byte runs).
  - Micro QR: 「日本語」 (M3) and 「日本語日本\」 under `Optimal` (a Kanji plan at M3).
  - rMQR: 「日本語のテキストです、ようこそ」 and 「~/設定/日本語のテキスト」 under `Optimal`.
  - Structured Append: 「こんにちは世界、QRコードの分割テストです。」 × 3 under `Optimal` at versions up to 3-M (a Kanji set, parity 176), and the same with `EciMode.Utf8` (a UTF-8 set, parity 6).
  - Japanese text on phones: scan ECI 26 UTF-8 (「日本語～」) and Kanji with no ECI (「日本語」) in Standard QR with the iPhone Camera app and Google Lens and the Android QR scanner and Google Lens. In the last run (2026-10-01, iOS 26.5 and Android 17) the iPhone apps read both and Android read only ECI 26 UTF-8, which is why Standard QR writes UTF-8 by default and Kanji only on request (Phase 6). Google ML Kit documents that it does not recognize QR codes "generated in the ECI mode", but Android 17 read ECI 26. A release where Android stops reading it is a finding about the default output. Micro QR and rMQR are scanned with Denso Wave's 「クルクル - QRコードリーダー」, because neither phone's own scanner reads them.
- `PackageValidationBaselineVersion` set to `2.0.0` in both packed projects. The csproj comments already say there is no baseline until 2.0.0 ships and to set it then
- `SkiaSharp.QrCode` 2.0.0 stays an empty metapackage. `tools/check_package_deps.cs` asserts the graph after pack, as it does today
- Version bump: `tools/bump_version.cs` parses only `X.Y.Z`, so going from `2.0.0-preview.4` to `2.0.0` needs either a hand edit of `Directory.Build.props` and the README install lines or a tool that first learns prerelease versions. Decide inside the phase (the tool already prints the manual instruction). The tool also does not compile: `error CS0106` on a `static readonly` field declared among top-level statements, broken since the core split and unnoticed because nothing in CI runs it. The preview bumps in this line were done by hand. Fixing or deleting it is a separate change from the API work
- GitHub release notes lead with the migration table link. The Playground redeploys from the same tag

## Progress log

Entries are appended per phase: what was done, what was learned, and the benchmark delta or an explicit statement that no hot path moved.

### Phase 1, announced removals (2026-09-06)

Done. `Compression`, both throwing `GetRequiredBufferSize` methods and all seven parameter list `Create*` overloads are gone. The ten remaining `Create*` entry points and `TryGetRequiredBufferSize` take `in {Sym}CodeGeneratorOptions options = default`, so `CreateQrCode(text, ecc)` still compiles and now resolves to the options path. Core drops from 34 exported types to 33, `QRCodeGenerator` from 10 public methods to 5, `MicroQRCodeGenerator` from 8 to 4. Both `PublicAPI.approved.txt` files are regenerated, and the renderer listing is unchanged. 119 call sites migrated across tests, benchmarks, Playground, samples and `tools/QRInteropFixtures`. `docs/migration.md` gains an "announced removals" section with the argument-to-property table and the `-1` trap. The spec's API-direction paragraphs move to past tense, and its exception-disagreement record becomes a lesson. The full suite passes: 17,609 tests, 0 failures, both target frameworks.

Lessons. [qrcode-symbologies.md](../specs/qrcode-symbologies.md) records three:

- differential tests die with their reference and had to be converted to frozen values before the deletion
- `required` members make the implicit constructor `[Obsolete]`, which looks like an announced removal in the approved listing but is not one (`IconData()` was on this plan's removal list in error)
- the one break the compiler could not find was `requestedVersion: -1` against a `QRCodeVersionRange` that rejects `-1` by design.

Benchmarks: not run, no hot path moved. The removed overloads were forwarding wrappers. The remaining options path and the private `Create*Core` methods are byte-identical. The only benchmark files touched are decode-fixture builders (`BuildModules` and similar), outside any measured method.

The Playground was verified by hand because `QrInterop` changed: a published Debug WASM build encoded through all four paths the change touches, Standard QR automatic (v5), Standard QR pinned (v10, 65×65), Micro QR automatic (M2, 17×17) and Micro QR pinned (M4, 21×21). Decode was not re-checked because no decode call site changed.

Two items stay out of this phase. `QRCodeCalculatedSize`'s public constructor and `IsValid` are in the removals table but belong to Phase 3's value-kind unification, and D1 (the `string` convenience overloads) stays with Phase 2 and the other shape decisions.

### Phase 2, renames (2026-09-06)

Done. Both rename tables and D1 are applied: the four `string` convenience overloads are gone, so every generator has two `Create` methods (span, span-plus-destination) and `TryGetRequiredBufferSize`. `Vector2Slim` is internal and moved under `FeatherQR.SkiaSharp.Internals`. The `Internals/RmQr` folder is `Internals/RmQR`, matching its namespace and its `MicroQR` / `StandardQR` siblings. Core stays at 33 exported types and the rendering package drops to 25 (`Vector2Slim`), 58 across both. 216 files changed. The full suite passes (17,609 tests, both target frameworks), and the passing golden-pixel tests show that the mechanical rewrite changed only names. The Playground was re-verified in WASM (QR v5 automatic, QR pinned v10, Micro QR M2, rMQR R9x139) and its committed API page regenerated. `docs/migration.md` gains the rename table and a runnable replacement script. The naming rule is now recorded in [qrcode-symbologies.md](../specs/qrcode-symbologies.md) under "Public API direction", because this plan is deleted at the end.

Test names followed the API: `CreateQrCode_*` / `CreateMicroQRCode_*` test methods became `Create_*`, `QRCodeRendererRunMergeParityTest` became `SymbolRendererRunMergeParityTest`, and `QRCodeSegmentationTest` became `QRSegmentationTest`. Benchmark class names stay, because they identify historical BenchmarkDotNet reports, and `QRCodeSegmentationEncode` reads as English, not as a type reference.

Lessons. The spec records two: PowerShell's `-ne` is case-insensitive, so a case-only rename silently writes nothing. A blanket identifier rewrite reaches third-party API with the same spelling (`QRCoder.QRCodeGenerator.ECCLevel` in the comparator benchmarks was renamed with ours, and only the compiler caught it). A third concerns process: `@(@('a','b'))` collapses to a two-element array in PowerShell, so `$pair[0]` became a character and `String.Replace(char, char)` corrupted three test files. They were restored from HEAD (Phase 1 was committed) and the rules re-applied. Build replacement pairs as `[pscustomobject]` or ordered dictionaries, never as nested arrays.

Benchmarks: not run, no hot path moved. The phase only renames. The two call sites that changed shape (`string` overload callers) now bind to the span overload the string one forwarded to.

### Phase 3, shape unification (2026-09-06)

Done. `QRCodeCalculatedSize` is a non-positional `readonly record struct` with an internal constructor and get-only properties, like its two siblings: the public constructor, `IsValid`, the `init` setters and deconstruction are gone, and `ToString()`, `==` and `IEquatable<T>` stay (the first cut removed those too, see the rework note below). `GradientOptions` is a `sealed record class` that copies the arrays it is given, returns them as `ReadOnlySpan<T>` (`ColorPositions` empty, not null, when evenly distributed) and compares by element. The generated equality it replaces compared arrays by reference, so identical gradients were unequal and `Default` was publicly mutable. `IconData` is `sealed` with `init`-only properties. `QRCodeData`, `MicroQRCodeData`, `RmQRCodeData` and the three image builders are `sealed`. The new `TypeShapeTest` (36 cases) guards all of it. The full suite passes: 17,659 tests, both target frameworks. This is the API-final point for the cleanup, and `2.0.0-preview.3` can be tagged from here.

One plan item was already true. The `*DecodeInfo` member order was listed as inconsistent, but all three declare `Status, Version, EccLevel, [MaskPattern,] ErrorsCorrected` in that order, with matching constructor order. The approved API listing sorts members by type and name, and reading it instead of the source produced the claim. The test now checks the member set, which is the property that matters.

An adversarial review (2026-09-06) led to a second round of rework. Three reviewers and three refutation passes found the same mistake elsewhere: demoting the six result values to plain structs had also removed `ToString` (a logged size printed as the type name), `==` and `IEquatable<T>` (measured 64 bytes of boxing per `Equals`), while `ModuleRect` and the three generator options next to them stayed `readonly record struct`. `IconData` had lost `with` as `GradientOptions` had. Both are `record`s again, with the wrong members (public constructor, `init` setters on results) still removed, so the public surface only gains `IEquatable<T>` on seven types. The spec records the rule: remove the member that is wrong, not the enclosing kind. `with` is offered for the members that carry no invariant, and that line is now documented. `GradientOptions.Direction` is `init`. `Colors` and `ColorPositions` are not, because `with` assigns one member at a time and those two must agree in length, so an `init` colour list would let a caller build a gradient whose stops no longer match and find out only when it is drawn. A span property can take an `init` accessor, and checking that this lets the mismatch through settled it. `IconData` needs no exception because none of its members validate against another at construction, which is why the two option types differ. A `WithColors` wither that carried the direction and stops for the caller was written and then dropped: it saved only two copied-over arguments (a mismatched colour count throws either way), and nothing in the repository recolours an existing gradient, so it was API on anticipation. A code comment where the methods were gives the reason.

The migration guide exposed a defect in the type. The recolour recipe had to read `options.ColorPositions.IsEmpty ? null : options.ColorPositions.ToArray()` because `GradientOptions` returned colours as spans and took them as arrays, and spelled "no stops" as empty on the way out and `null` on the way in. The constructor now takes spans, empty on both sides, so the line is `new GradientOptions([…], options.Direction, options.ColorPositions)`. Arrays still convert implicitly, so no existing call site changed. `null` can no longer be passed for the stops, and an empty array now means "evenly distributed" instead of throwing. Documenting the unreadable line would have shipped the asymmetry.

Four more findings from the same round were fixed with it. The migration guide's recolour recipe silently dropped `ColorPositions`. It now carries them and says why the omission is invisible. `README.md` still described `GetRequiredBufferSize` as deprecated but present, a release out of date. `ShapeHierarchies_StayOpen_AndTheBuilderBaseDoesNot` ran `All()` over the non-public constructors, which a public constructor empties, so it passed vacuously for the violation it names. It now asserts that the public constructor list is empty, and fails when the constructor is made public. The immutability wording claimed the colour array was unreachable, which `MemoryMarshal.GetReference` disproves with no `unsafe` and no opt-in, so the documented guarantee is "immutable through the API". The first attempt named this escape hatch in the XML remarks, which was wrong for the reason a library does not caveat reflection: it is noise to a caller who wants a gradient, and nobody can close it. The finding was about the absolute claim, which a later change could have relied on to skip the defensive copy. The qualifier alone fixes that, and a code comment beside the property gives the reasoning. The last finding, that `GradientOptions` is no longer System.Text.Json-serializable, was accepted: through 1.x it serialized only incidentally, emitting `SKColor`'s `{Alpha,Red,Green,Blue}` shape, which no caller wants persisted, and the Playground, the only JSON consumer here, already maps to its own DTO of `#RRGGBB` strings. A `JsonConverter` would add a System.Text.Json dependency to the netstandard builds and change the packed dependency graph, which is not worth it before someone asks with a use case. At the maintainer's request this reasoning is a code comment beside the property, not in the XML docs or the migration guide.

A maintainer review led to one round of rework. The first cut made `GradientOptions` a plain `sealed class`, which silently removed `with`, an idiom the three generator options structs still support and the README teaches. The defect called for restoring the record with private arrays: the bug was the public array, not the record, and a private array makes the record's shallow copy safe. `Direction` is the only `init` member, so `with { Direction = … }` compiles and `with { Colors = … }` does not: colours define the gradient, and direction is the cheap variation. `PrintMembers` is hand-written because the generated one would print a `ReadOnlySpan<T>` member as a type name and must compile on four target frameworks.

Two kinds of type keep their shape. `ModuleRect` keeps its public constructor and `init` members: it is a geometry value a caller may also build (for tests or their own layout), not an answer the library returns, so the `Try`-result rule does not apply. The generator options structs keep `init` because a caller builds those.

Benchmarks: not run, no hot path moved. The only behavioural change is `GradientOptions` copying two small arrays once at construction, outside any measured path. The renderer reaches the same arrays through an internal property. The Playground was not re-verified because `QrInterop` did not change, and the committed golden PNGs in `RenderingApprovalTest` cover the gradient rendering path.

### Phases 1-3 pre-PR adversarial review (2026-09-07)

Done. Five parallel reviewers covered the whole `main...api_break` diff, and three-verifier refutation rounds then checked the claims with a design consequence. The fixes follow in severity order.

The branch did not compile in Release. `QRCodeDecoderRoundTripTest.cs:150` sat inside `#if !DEBUG` and still called the removed parameter list overload, so `dotnet build -c Release`, the first step of CI, failed. Debug built clean, so the "full suite green, both target frameworks" claim in the Phase 1-3 entries above was Debug-only, and `Decode_CharSpanDestination_IsAllocationFree`, the only zero-allocation guard on the span decode path, had never run on this branch. It now runs and passes.

The `string` overload removal rested on a false premise, and it broke the option structs as well. D1 recorded that `string` converts implicitly to `ReadOnlySpan<char>` on all four target frameworks. It converts on three. The conversion is compiler-synthesized, not an operator on `System.String`, and when `ReadOnlySpan<T>` comes from the `System.Memory` package instead of the framework (the netstandard2.0 asset, which .NET Framework 4.6.2+ binds), only C# 14 synthesizes it. Every version through 13 reports `CS1503`. This was measured with a consumer project: the same consumer compiles and runs against the published `SkiaSharp.QrCode` 1.2.0 and against a pack of `main`, and fails against this branch. The larger problem lay underneath. `init` accessors need C# 9, so on netstandard2.0 (default C# 7.3) and netstandard2.1 (default C# 8.0) the option structs became unconfigurable once Phase 1 removed the parameter lists: `with`, a constructor, property assignment and implicit conversion were all refused, leaving only `Create(text.AsSpan(), ecc)` with defaults. All three option structs and `IconData` now have a constructor that assigns through the same `init` accessors, so equality is unchanged and validation is identical on the three option structs. `IconData` differs in one place: its constructor rejects a null `Icon`, because compilers with no nullable analysis reach that route. `IconData`, found one round later, is the sharper case: its only other public routes are two factories that both hardcode `ImageIconShape`, so `ImageTextIconShape` and any caller-written `IconShape` (the documented extension point, and the spelling the README teaches) were unreachable below C# 9. `TypeShapeTest` states the rule, not the instance: every settable option has a constructor parameter of the same type, and only a `required` member may be mandatory, because an option reachable only through an object initializer is unreachable below C# 9.

Lessons. [qrcode-symbologies.md](../specs/qrcode-symbologies.md) records four, so they survive this plan's deletion. A claim about consumer compilation cannot be checked from the library's own build, which compiles at C# 14 and so proves nothing. It needs a consumer project at the SDK-default language version, preferably one that also runs. A blanket rename sweep reaches the repository's own released package, not only third-party API: `samples/Dotfiles/FinderPatternAlwaysBlack.cs` pins `SkiaSharp.QrCode@1.0.0` and had its calls rewritten to 2.0.0 names, the trap the Phase 2 lesson records for QRCoder, one directory over. A differential test whose reference is deleted becomes a tautology instead of a failure: `ArgumentErrorPrecedenceTest.OptionsAndParameterList_ReportTheSameArgumentError` survived the sweep comparing a call with a textually identical copy of itself, a case the Phase 1 lesson predicted for the three test classes it converted to frozen values but missed here.

The fourth widens the Phase 2 case-only-rename lesson. Phase 2 left one prose mention of `Internals/RmQr`, and the sweep for it also found twenty-nine spec-map links to `Internals/StandardQr/` that had been stale since long before this branch (the folder was already `StandardQR` on `main`). Each is a 404 on GitHub and on any case-sensitive checkout, and a link checker on Windows reports them as fine because the filesystem is case-insensitive. Resolving each link against `git ls-files` instead of the disk found them. A case-only rename needs a case-sensitive oracle, and on this machine the index is the only one.

The review also fixed:

- six `<paramref name="data"/>` tags naming a parameter called `bitmap`, which shipped 24 `CS1734` warnings into the published XML docs
- `GradientOptions.Equals`, which could regress to comparing stop counts with every gradient test still green, so the missing equivalence classes are now asserted (proven by mutation)
- the Standard QR `ArgumentException` for an undefined ECC level and Micro QR's quiet zone upper bound, which both lost their only test with `SizingExceptionContractTest`
- `TypeWithNoExtensionPoint_IsSealed`, a hand-maintained list of eight types that now sweeps both assemblies against a declared set of four extension points
- three benchmarks that became exact duplicates when the overloads they were paired with were removed
- all six `samples/Dotfiles` entries, which had been left half-migrated (`Sample.cs` gets its namespaces and project reference like the rest, but as a directives-only template with no body it still does not build, as on `main`)
- stale prose across `standardqr-encoder.md`, `rmqr-encoder.md`, all three spec maps, `README.md` and `docs/migration.md`, including a dead link, two spec-map rows pointing into the wrong package, and two test method names the `\b`-anchored sweep could not match.

The committed Playground API page was regenerated too. It was three commits stale, so it showed none of the new constructors, and since Phase 2 it had carried 347 SourceLink URLs pinned to an unmerged commit, which `release.yaml` and the Playground README both forbid in the committed copy: `--source-links` belongs to the release job alone because only that job builds at the tag. `main` carries none, and now neither does the page.

Benchmarks: not run, no hot path moved. The option struct constructors are additive and run only where a caller builds an option set. The `GradientOptions.PrintMembers` change removes a boxing conversion on a diagnostic path. An ad-hoc differential sweep during the review (31,296 encode/decode and 1,728 rendering cases against a build of `main`, not a committed artifact) found zero differences, so the "renames only" claim of Phases 1-3 is now measured instead of asserted.

### Phase 4, symbol geometry (2026-09-07)

Done. D3 is decided and recorded above. The core gains two shared, library-built record structs, `ImagePoint` (`float X`, `float Y`) and `SymbolCorners` (`TopLeft`, `TopRight`, `BottomRight`, `BottomLeft`, `IsEmpty`). All three `*DecodeInfo` types gain a `Corners` member, attached through an internal `WithCorners` so the matrix decoders know nothing of geometry. One internal helper, `SymbolGeometry`, projects the four grid corners through whichever mapping the decoder sampled with (a `PerspectiveTransform`, Micro QR's affine `origin + u·col + v·row` frame, or the mesh-anchored transform Standard QR builds when the piecewise mesh sampled). Standard QR and Micro QR carry one extra bit out of their mirror retry (whether the transposed matrix decoded) and swap `TopRight`/`BottomLeft` on it. rMQR's frames already swap axes, so its transform is in symbol order. Core goes from 33 to 35 exported types. The rendering package is unchanged. `SymbolCornersTest` (axis-aligned to a tenth of a pixel, 90°/180°/270° and oblique rotation, mirror with reversed winding, keystone per version, matrix decode and the three failure classes empty, luminance and bitmap overloads agree) and new `TypeShapeTest` cases cover it. The full suite passes at 17,813 tests across both target frameworks (17,831 in Release). README, `docs/migration.md` (additive section), the shared contract in [qrcode-symbologies.md](../specs/qrcode-symbologies.md) and the per-symbology notes in the Standard QR and rMQR decoder records are updated. The Playground is untouched (showing the outline there is a follow-up).

The first accuracy measurement, superseded by the review round below, gave half a module for flat, rotated and mirrored captures on all three symbologies, and under keystone half a module for Standard QR with an alignment pattern and one module for Micro QR and rMQR. Two of those statements failed adversarial review: the keystone cases had only exercised versions below the mesh threshold (the mesh needs version 14 and up, not 7), and the Micro QR and rMQR rotation/keystone bounds were measured at a single lucky angle and a single lenient tilt.

In the review round (2026-09-07), five reviewer lenses ran in parallel, then three refutation agents per surviving claim. Six claims reached the shortlist, none was refuted by two of three, and all six were fixed against a red test or a measured assertion.
- The mesh path reported an unvalidated transform. When the piecewise mesh sampled (version 14+), `Corners` came from the global 4-point transform the decode never validated: 18 to 30 modules off at the bottom-right on a keystoned version 16. `MeshAnchoredTransform` fixes it with a quad fit through the three finder centres and the mesh's bottom-right lattice node. Bilinear extrapolation of the outer mesh cell, tried first, left the top-left 0.6 to 0.75 module short. Keystone tests at that pass covered versions 2, 7, 20, 25 and 30 at half a module (2, 5, 7, 10, 14, 20, 25 and 30 after the later passes).
- A half-pixel shift was a bias. `SymbolGeometry` added 0.5 px on the theory that the decoders sample in an "integer = pixel centre" convention, but the finder centres already use the edge convention (exclusive run ends), so every finder-anchored corner sat half a pixel outside the symbol. The shift is removed, and a tenth-of-a-pixel axis-aligned test checks it. Alignment-anchored (`AlignmentPatternFinder` refines Y with `+0.5f`) and sub-finder-anchored (rMQR dark-run centre, about −0.75) corners keep sub-pixel residuals of their own. Unifying those anchor conventions is a follow-up, not a corner bug.
- Micro QR oblique rotation is not half a module. The finder-axis sweep scores integer-pixel runs, flat for ±3–4° around the truth, and the first 1° candidate that decodes wins. Corners 13 to 19 modules from the finder move 0.2 to 0.9 module at 8, 16 and 32 px per module alike. The contract is relaxed to about a module for oblique Micro QR, and tests at 8°, 20°, 60°, 75° and a rotated mirror check it.
- rMQR keystone exceeds a module on short symbols: one of the two far corners is 1.22 to 1.24 modules off at 3 to 4 % on R11x59 (the shear search under-recovers the column-axis lean and the first decoding transform wins). The first quoted figures, 1.27 to 1.30, included the half-pixel shift. The contract says a module and a half from 3 % up on short symbols. Tests cover R7x43, R11x59 and R17x139 at 4 %, and the spec record no longer names one corner as the worst (it is the bottom-left on R11x59 at 3 to 4 % and the top-right on R7x43, neither "top-right" as first written nor "bottom-left" as corrected).
- Negative tests were too weak. A mutant that attached corners on every terminal status passed the whole suite, because the only negative test used a blank image, which exits as `NotDetected` before any attach site. `DestinationTooSmall` (one-char destination) and `DataUncorrectable` (a painted-over data block) cases now assert `Corners.IsEmpty` on all three symbologies.
- Docs stated intended behaviour, not measured behaviour. Accuracy text in `SymbolCorners`, the shared contract, the rMQR and Standard QR decoder records and the migration guide now states the measured envelope, and the "integer = pixel centre" sentence is gone. A second reviewer pass on the docs caught the contract quoting the tested keystone range as the decoder's envelope, and three copies of one measurement with three different numbers. The keystone tests now run at 12 % on versions 2 and 5, 6 to 8 % on 7 and 10, 5 to 6 % from 14 up, and Micro QR at 2, 4, 5 and 8 % (most versions decode further on that scene and hold the bound there too), and every figure has one source. A third pass found the rMQR figures measured before the half-pixel shift was removed. They are re-measured from the shipped code.

In the branch-wide review round (2026-09-09), four reviewer lenses covered the whole branch, then three refutation agents per shortlisted claim. Five claims survived at 3/3, one ("the corner tolerances are one rasterizer rounding from red") was dropped at 2/3 refuted, and the merge from `main` was independently verified to have lost nothing. Its findings, by importance:
- The Playground drew the outline in the wrong place for EXIF-rotated photos. `imageOrientation: 'none'` does not suppress EXIF (it is a legacy alias for `from-image`), and `flipY` applies the tag too, so no option value opts out. Skia decodes the stored pixels, the browser displays the oriented ones, and the width/height guard only catches the tags that swap dimensions: for tags 2, 3 and 4 the outline landed on blank paper under a confident caption, and a mirrored photo was reported "not mirrored". The fix reads the tag with `SKCodec.EncodedOrigin` (which Skia parses and then ignores) and maps the corners through it, so all eight orientations draw correctly, measured within 2 px of the symbol on every tag, and the winding describes what the viewer sees.
- Two overlapping decodes crossed their results. Pasting twice, or dropping during a decode, left the canvas showing the first image while the result line described the second, and leaked the loser's `ImageBitmap`. It reproduced at a 20 ms gap with no artificial delay, because a small image resolves faster than a large one. A generation token fixes it and also closes the bitmap the superseded run made.
- The half-module accuracy figure held only from 8 px per module up. The bottom-right corner is anchored on the alignment pattern, whose centre resolves to about a pixel at any module size, so its error is near-constant in pixels (4.09 px at 6 px per module, 3.63 at 8, 3.94 at 12) and grows in modules as the capture coarsens: 0.68 module at 6, and 0.58 on a flat, axis-aligned version 2 at 2 px per module, where version 1 measures exactly zero because it is finder-anchored. No minimum density was documented, and `FinderPatternFinder` calls 3 px per module the bottom of the envelope. The contract now states the density, and four rows check the pixel bound.
- Any version can silently get version 1's looser fit. When the bottom-right alignment pattern is not found, `BuildGridTransform` falls back to the finders-only parallelogram on every version, error correction still returns `Success`, and one erased module is enough to trigger it (v2 at 3 % keystone is 1.00 module out and v10 at 1 % is 1.11). The contract named version 1 as the only loose case. It now names both, and three rows assert that the fallback is in use, not only that the corner is within bounds.
- A third mirrored attach site was untested. In the mirrored branch of Micro QR's arbitrary-orientation sweep, dropping its `transposed` flag swapped TopRight with BottomLeft by about 24 modules and reversed the winding, and the whole suite stayed green. An 8° row fills the last empty cell in the mapping × mirror table.
- The round also fixed these: a page-wide paste took clipboards that carry a bitmap alongside text (Excel, Word), and after the first fix took nothing when focus sat on a checkbox. A synchronous WASM decode froze the page for up to 4.3 s with no busy state, and the first busy state did not paint because a single `requestAnimationFrame` resolves before the frame it schedules. A preview failure un-hid the figure still holding the previous image and its outline. The sample now exits non-zero when a scene stops decoding, guards its canvas bounds, and states its keystone arithmetic correctly.

One fix was reverted. The mesh corner anchor was changed to the bottom-right-most detected lattice node, because the comment claimed the anchor was a node the decode had validated, which was not guaranteed. Against the unchanged code, on every mesh version and tilt and with the diagonal pattern erased, the two give byte-identical corners: the mesh's refinement rounds have already re-predicted that node from a homography through the nodes it found. Code whose effect no test can observe is worse than an accurate comment, so the plumbing came out and the comment now says what the anchor is. The reviewer's related point stands: a comment's claim must be made true or withdrawn. `SymbolCornersTest` has 62 cases after the round. The third pass added a mirrored keystone on the version-20 mesh path and Micro QR keystones at 5 and 8 % plus a mirrored 8 %, the only rows that reach the mesh's and the single-finder perspective search's attach sites. A mutant dropping the transposed flag at either site had passed the suite.

Lessons. The spec's contract paragraph and the decoder records hold three. An accuracy figure measured at one angle and one tilt is not a bound: the first draft's "half a module" for Micro QR was true at 20° and false at 8°, 17° and 60°, and rMQR's "one module" was true at 2 % and false at 3 %. Sweep the parameter before writing the number. Read a decoder's internal coordinate convention off the code that produces the anchors, not the code that consumes them (the `(int)(x + 0.5f)` samplers looked like a pixel-centre convention and were a rounding). A negative test must reach the site it guards: a blank image exits at detection, so it never tested the `Success` gate. The follow-ups are a sub-degree refit of the winning single-finder frame after decode (which would tighten Micro QR and rMQR to Standard QR's bound) and the alignment/sub-finder anchor convention.

Benchmarks: no regression, with a lesson about measuring. The first before/after pair ran while builds and the test suite ran concurrently, and the matrix-path rows moved +30 to +50 %, impossible for a change that touches the matrix path only by widening an `out` struct from 20 to 52 bytes. Re-measured with the sources stashed to HEAD on an idle machine (ShortRun, both classes back to back), Standard QR matrix rows moved +0.8 % / +1.0 % / +5.3 % / +1.7 % / +1.2 %, the image row −1.1 %, span rows −0.6 % / −0.7 % / +1.0 % / −2.9 % / −3.3 %, rMQR rows −2.9 % to −8.6 % and one +2.2 % with a 7 µs error bar. Allocations were identical on every row. One row crossed the gate: `QR_Byte_V40_H (Span)` at +12.1 % in the clean run. Its string twin, which does strictly more work, moved +1.2 % in the same run, and an immediate re-run of the two V40_H rows put both at +15–19 % over the same baseline, moving together: the 100 µs, RS-heavy version-40 cases drift that much between ShortRun launches on this machine, and nothing in the change can cause it there. It is recorded as noise with that evidence. A MediumRun on those two rows is the next step if certainty is wanted. After the review round (mesh-anchored transform, shift removed), the same two classes re-run on an idle machine against that clean pre-review run gave every Standard QR row −3 to −11 % (image row 33.3 → 31.0 µs, V40_H span 112 → 99 µs, both twins moving together) and every rMQR row −2 to −9 %, with allocations identical on all rows. Nothing crossed the +10 % gate.

The corners are also drawn (2026-09-08). They were listed as a follow-up and then done, because nobody checks a geometry feature they cannot see. `samples/Dotfiles/DecodeCorners.cs` decodes a flat, a rotated, a mirrored and a keystoned capture of the same symbol and writes each with the reported outline, the `TopLeft` marker and the four labels drawn on it, so the symbol-frame naming and the reversed winding are visible side by side. The migration guide and the README point to it. The Playground's decode panel, which showed only a line of text, now draws the image on a canvas with the same outline and says which way the winding runs. It also takes an image pasted anywhere on the page or dropped on the panel, and a checkbox turns the overlay off for anyone who only wants to read the code. Four details had to be right. The page maps the corners through the file's EXIF orientation before drawing, because the library decodes the stored pixels and a browser displays the oriented ones. The payload carries both the tag (read with `SKCodec.EncodedOrigin`) and the decoded size, so a residual mismatch drops the overlay instead of drawing it in the wrong place. The canvas is sized in CSS pixels and scaled by the device pixel ratio, with the corners mapped into that space. The first version drew at the image's own resolution and let CSS resize the canvas, so the browser stretched a small symbol and the outline looked soft. Paste is page-wide but skips a target that takes typed text, because a clipboard from Excel or Word carries a bitmap alongside the text and claiming it would lose the user's paste. Drop is scoped to the panel, because the logo field takes dropped images too and a page-wide target would swallow those. A published WASM build verified all four captures, a Micro QR pasted from the clipboard, a mirrored capture dropped on the panel, the toggle both ways, a text paste into the content field (not intercepted), a non-image drop, and an image with no code (preview shown, honest caption, no stale outline). The sample also found that the `SKPath` recipe the migration guide gave for drawing the quadrilateral is obsolete under the SkiaSharp 4.148 the library pins, so the guide and the sample now use `SKPathBuilder`.

Two additions wait for a request. A derived `IsMirrored` was not added because the winding already carries it and the public-API rule wants a request first.
