The five rounds also made smaller corrections. Three `SKCanvas.Render` size overloads still opened with "with the default colors" on methods that take colours. The renderer's new `codeColor` doc said the value is unused without naming one to pass, and "unused" is conditional: `GradientDirection.None` and a `gradientOptions` that turns out to be `null` both paint it. The builder half of the rule was undocumented while [migration.md](../../../docs/migration.md) promises that chaining these setters "does what reading them suggests". `WithGradient` wins over a later `WithCodeColor`, and both setters now say so. The migration guide's "before" line called the type `SymbolRenderer`, which did not exist until this release (`QRCodeRenderer` did, as the same file's rename table says). "The extensions are unchanged" became "keep their signatures", because their bodies did change. The three gradient samples had lost the comment saying why they pass a colour, and carry a shorter one again. This plan's Phase 3b prose still described the two parameters in the present tense. The rMQR spec's signature block, edited in this change for the colours, still omitted `finderPatternShape`. This entry claimed "two rMQR tests" for two call sites in one.

Lessons. A surviving mutant is worth more than a passing test: three of the four tests this change shipped were the only ones in the suite that could catch their mutants, and the one hole was in the path the class had explained away in a comment instead of covering. A comment that says why something is not tested should name the test that covers it. Otherwise it is an assumption. When a change makes an argument required, list the spellings a caller can write for it, not only the values: `null` and `default` were the same under `SKColor?` and are not under `SKColor`, and only one of them is a compile error. A decision record is only as reliable as the measurement it quotes, so a claim about "the three overloads" must be tried on three overloads.

### The size overloads' forwarding is pinned (2026-09-13)

Done. F9 adds `SymbolRendererSizeOverloadForwardingTest`, 18 cases, tests only. No production code changed. Sixteen cases take one option at a time through a `SKCanvas.Render(data, width, height, …)` overload and through the area overload over `SKRect.Create(0, 0, width, height)`, the rectangle the size overload builds, and require the two to be byte-identical. The seventeenth and eighteenth sample an icon's border ring. Each case has a control against the same render with the option unset, so a comparison cannot pass by both sides drawing nothing. All ten arguments a size overload forwards now fail a mutant: the F4 review covered the two colours and the two axes, and this class covers `clearColor`, `iconData`, `moduleShape`, `moduleSizePercent`, `gradientOptions` and `finderPatternShape` on every symbology that has them. All twenty-three mutants run were killed: seventeen on the size forwards and the icon draw, and six on the area forwards, which the controls also cover.

The controls also test the area overloads, which was not the intent. Each case compares the option's render with the same render without it, and the size overload reaches the pixels through the area overload, so an argument the area overload drops makes those two identical and the control fails. Measured: dropping `finderPatternShape`, `moduleSizePercent` or `iconData` from the Standard QR area forward, `moduleShape` from Micro QR's, or `gradientOptions` or `finderPatternShape` from rMQR's each fails a case here. One class covers both forwarding layers, and `CanvasExtension_ForwardsTheFinderShape` is no longer the only test of the area overloads' trailing arguments.

The clear colour is observable only on a canvas bigger than the symbol, which is why nothing had caught it. A size overload asks for a rectangle at the origin, and the background covers exactly that rectangle, so on a canvas no larger than the requested size every cleared pixel is painted over. Every existing test caller of a size overload draws onto a canvas of exactly that size. The new class renders 200x200 onto 260x260, where the clear colour survives in the band on two sides, and hardcoding it then fails on all three symbologies. This answers the F9 row's question: the mutant was uncaught, not equivalent, and is cheap to catch once the canvas has room.

The icon's border was the one line of the F4 change no test could distinguish. `SymbolRenderer` passes the background colour to `IconShape.Draw`, which fills the ring between the border rect and the image with it. Every icon test in the suite draws on white, so substituting `SKColors.White` in that call repainted white with white and changed nothing. `Render_Icon_PaintsItsBorderInTheBackgroundColor` samples a point midway across the ring on the left side, where the image never reaches, on gold and on teal, with a white render as the control that the sample point is the ring, not the field around it.

Lessons. A forwarding method with no logic is the easiest thing in a library to leave untested, and the most mechanical to test: the assertion is always "this entry point draws what the one it delegates to draws". An argument that cannot change the output under the conditions every test uses looks the same as an argument that is not forwarded, so testing it starts with finding the condition that makes it visible. These holes hide in the suite's uniform habits: every icon test used a white background, and every size-overload caller used a canvas the size of its request, so two arguments were invisible for the same reason.

Benchmark delta: not measured, because no production code changed.

### The builder's setters are pinned against each other (2026-09-14)

Done. F6 adds `SymbolImageBuilderOptionInteractionTest`, 98 cases, tests only. No production code changed. Ten options, one per field the base builder holds, are crossed with the four setters where the cross-assignment sweep found most survivors (`WithQuietZone`, `WithModulePixelSize`, `WithSize`, `WithFormat`), minus the self-pairs where overwriting is the contract. Each pair is asserted twice: the option still changes the image when the later setter is called after it, and the two orders produce the same image. Three more classes of case cover the rest: `WithFormat` encoding the format and quality it names (magic bytes for PNG, JPEG and WebP, and two JPEG qualities differing in size), the format and quality surviving each of the ten styling setters called after them, and the premise that every option in the table changes the image on its own, without which a survival case could pass by both sides drawing nothing. The two `FluentAPI_*` tests in `QRCodeImageBuilderTest`, which chained five to nine setters and asserted `IsNotNull` and the dimensions, now assert the format's magic bytes, the background colour at the corner, that the symbol still decodes to its content, and that the gradient changed the image. All nine mutants run were killed, including the one the F6 row named: `WithFormat` ignoring both its arguments failed 13 cases where it used to fail none. The full suite passes: 18,917 tests, both target frameworks.

The quiet zone is invisible whenever the padding has its colour, so a whole family of these pairs could not be written the obvious way. The first cut of the table failed one case, `QuietZone` against `WithModulePixelSize`, and it was not a defect: the quiet zone is drawn in the background colour, and the leftover canvas is also padded in the background colour when no clear colour is set, so a symbol with a one-module quiet zone centred on a larger canvas is pixel-identical to the same symbol with four. Every case therefore renders with a clear colour set, which separates the padding from the quiet zone and makes the field observable. The option that sets a clear colour uses a second colour so that it stays observable itself.

Lessons. A cross-assignment survives in a setter that changes no pixels of its own, because the usual assertion about it checks shape (the dimensions, that bytes came back), and a shape assertion cannot see a colour or a module shape going missing. The cheap general form is two properties over a table, not one test per pair: the earlier option still reaches the output, and the two calls commute. Such a table needs its premise tested too, because a case comparing "with the option" against "without it" passes trivially once the option stops drawing anything.

Benchmark delta: not measured, because no production code changed.

### A NaN corner radius is refused at the constructor (2026-09-14)

Done. This is F7's remaining half. `RoundedRectangleModuleShape`, `RoundedRectangleFinderPatternShape` and `RoundedRectangleCircleFinderPatternShape` guard `cornerRadiusPercent` with `is not (>= 0f and <= 1f)` instead of `< 0 || > 1`, the negated form Phase 3b gave the builder, so NaN is refused where it used to construct and then draw a plain rectangle. `RoundedShapeCornerRadiusGuardTest` has 19 cases: NaN, both infinities and the two out-of-range values per constructor, the three in-range values that must still construct, and one case checking the guard's premise, that a 0.3 radius draws a different dark-sample count than a plain square, so the rectangle NaN used to produce was a downgrade, not a no-op. Exactly three cases were red before the fix (the NaN one per shape, because `+∞ > 1` and `−∞ < 0` were already caught), and all are green after. `docs/migration.md` gains a section. The approved API listings are unchanged, because no signature moved. The full suite passes: 18,759 tests, both target frameworks.

The two infinities that already worked kept this in the follow-ups table instead of making it obvious. A reader checking whether `< 0 || > 1` rejects garbage tries an infinity first, gets an exception, and stops. NaN is the only float value both comparisons answer "no" to, and the only one a caller reaches by accident, from a division by a zero dimension instead of by typing it.

Lessons. A range guard written as two positive comparisons has a hole whenever the type has NaN, and every test that probes the guard with an extreme instead of a non-value misses it. The consequence here was worse than the late throw the builder half of F7 fixed: Skia silently accepts the non-finite radius and degrades the round rect, so the result was a picture that did not match the request, with no diagnostic. Where a guard protects a drawing parameter, the useful test checks that the parameter changes the drawing at all.

Benchmark delta: not measured. The change is three constructor guards, off any hot path.

### The finder triple is chosen by its shape (2026-09-19)

Done. This is F10. `FinderPatternFinder.TrySelectBestThree` scored only the three neighbours in module-size order, by `spread / count`. It now scores every triple by its distance from a right isosceles triangle plus the relative module-size spread, with the confirmation count breaking ties. The confirmed-only compaction and the three-candidate early return are unchanged, and nothing new is rejected. The corpus symbol reads from its PNG and from its matrix rendered at 3 to 16 px/module. `StructuredAppendFixtureTest` loses its known-defect list and the guard that went with it. `FinderPatternSelectionTest` has 23 cases: the selection classes on synthetic candidate lists (fewer than three, exactly three whatever their shape, the F10 shape, every scan order of it, a geometry-and-size tie settled by count, perfect geometry at the wrong module size, an unconfirmed candidate with better geometry, two symbols, a rotated symbol with an interior false candidate), the corpus symbol per density, two symbols from this library's encoder that carry a confirmed false finder, with a guard that fails if a later encoder change removes it, and two symbols side by side. 15 of the 23 fail against the old selector. The rest guard classes the new score could have broken. The full suite passes: 21,573 tests, both target frameworks.

The first diagnosis was wrong, and the candidate list would have shown it at once. F10 was filed as a false top-right finder three modules inside the real one, from the distances the decode reported. The locator had found all three real finders, each confirmed on every scanned row of its band. The false candidate sat in the bottom-right quadrant, built from the alignment pattern's ring and two data modules, and the ordering step turned the wrong triple into a wrong corner. Every downstream number followed from that and pointed at the wrong component.

The defect was not limited to one fixture. A before/after differential sweep of 20,000 renders from this library's own encoder (flat, rotated, keystoned, both, and two symbols side by side, 3 to 12 px/module, all versions) lost nothing and gained 364. 13 of the 40 flat failures were this class, at versions 2 to 33. The rest are F11, identical before and after. Two symbols in one frame failed 337 times in 4,000: whenever both were rendered at the same density, every candidate measured the same size, the old score tied, and the chosen triple mixed the two symbols.

Lessons. A score that multiplies a tie-breaker by a quantity that can be exactly zero has no tie-breaker, and the input that makes it zero here, a render at a whole number of pixels per module, is the most ordinary input, so the bug hid behind a density boundary (at 3 and 4 px/module the false pattern is one scanned row tall and the confirmation filter removed it), not behind rarity. A window over a sorted list assumes the best answer is contiguous in the sort key. With ties, the order inside the tie is the scan order, and the correct triple was never scored. When a locator must choose a shape, score the shape.

Benchmark delta: the success path is unchanged, because three candidates return before any scoring. `QRCodeDecodeEndToEnd.Image_Byte_Url_V6_M_Decode` measured 33.15 → 33.54 µs (Span 32.62 → 32.77 µs), inside the ShortRun error, with identical allocations. The selection itself is now cubic where it was near-linear: 32 same-size candidates with no good triangle cost 21 µs against 72 ns, because the size bound prunes nothing there. That list does not occur in practice: salt-and-pepper noise images at 512 and 1024 px, the failure path, measured within ±1 % before and after (1,780 → 1,788 µs, 996 → 985, 1,967 → 1,947, 1,495 → 1,484).

### Edges are measured against edges of the same polarity (2026-09-19)

Done. F11, on the F10 branch, makes four changes to the Standard QR image path, all in `src/FeatherQR/Internals`.
- `QRImageDecoder.MeasureBothWays` pairs the dark ring's inner edge on one side of the finder with its outer edge on the other (6 modules, twice per line), instead of the two outer edges (7 modules).
- `ReadVersionDimension` reads the two version information copies from the matrix sampled at the estimated dimension, and a named version different from the estimate is tried before the runner-up. The version snap is also clamped to 1-40, so an estimate just past 177 modules no longer comes back `NotDetected`.
- `AlignmentPatternFinder` keeps the hit nearest the prediction and re-centres it on its own row. It checks light+dark run pairs against a per-direction run length derived from the grid axes, and requires the light ring at ±1 module as well as the dark ring at ±2.
- `TrySelectBestThree`'s tie tolerance went from 1e-3 to 0.05, applied in a second pass over the best score.

The tests are `Decode_HalfPixelOffsetRender_ReadsTheTrueVersion` (12 cases, ink spread and erosion, 10 red before), `Decode_SupersampledRotatedRender_ReadsTheTrueVersion` (12 cases through a new `SupersampledRenderer`, 10 red before and 2 controls), `VersionInformationReadTest` (47), `AlignmentPatternSelectionTest` (8, both kernels, 6 red before) and one more finder-selection case (red before). The full suite passes: 21,733 tests, both target frameworks.

The bias was an asymmetry, not noise. An outer-to-outer span carries each edge's shift, and grey edge pixels shift a dark-to-light edge and a light-to-dark edge in opposite directions, so more measurements do not average the error out: it is one pixel per span, +4.8 % at 3 px/module, whichever way the grey falls. Pairing edges of the same polarity cancels it by construction. Over 480 rotated renders it took the mean error from +0.4..+1.4 % to within ±0.3 % at every density. It did not narrow the spread (worst case still about 5.6 % at 3 px/module, from pixel quantization along a rotated ray), so the version information is read too: at 3 px/module near the axis the estimate can land 9 modules off.

Removing the bias exposed the alignment search, which had depended on it. With the unbiased module size, 11 rotated renders that used to read failed. None was a module-size error: in each, the alignment search found a false pattern or none, and its result moved when the module size moved by under 1 %. Three defects combined there. The search took the first hit in scan order (4931: a false pattern at x=195 accepted while the real one sat 0.1 px from the prediction at x=214.5 on the same row). It compared each run with the plain module size, although a row crosses a module rotated 45° √2 times longer. And each single run gained or lost the bloom pixel. The old, inflated module size happened to sit where bloomed dark runs and rotated runs both fit. The light-ring check was measured in three variants (8 of 8, at least 6 of 8, none), and strict won on all three sweeps. A bilinear sample for it was no better.

Sweeps of `main` against this branch (the F10 harness, 20,000 renders each):

| Sweep | `main` | Branch | Gained | Lost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Seeds 0, clean | 19,324 | 19,871 | 547 | 0 |
| Seeds 100000, clean | 19,326 | 19,884 | 558 | 0 |
| Seeds 100000, degraded (box blur, contrast, ±24 noise) | 17,716 | 18,378 | 679 | 17 |
| Pinned content, v3-v10, 3-6 px/module, keystone 0/3/6 %, 0-88° | 3,688 / 3,780 | 3,760 / 3,780 | 73 | 1 |

Flat renders read 4,000 of 4,000 on both clean seed sets. All 17 degraded losses are at 3 and 4 px/module, where the branch gains 232 (157 and 75) on the same sweep. There, blur leaves a light module one or two pixels wide, and every variant tried traded a handful of cases either way. The grid's one loss is v7 at 3 px/module, 6 % keystone, 20°.

Lessons. A measurement spanning a dark-to-light edge and a light-to-dark edge carries the binarization's asymmetry into its result, and averaging more of them does not remove it. Pair edges of the same polarity. A check calibrated against a biased input depends on the bias: the alignment tolerances worked because the module size passed to them was wrong in the direction they needed, and correcting it moved 11 renders from reading to failing before the checks were fixed. A symbol that states its own version beats any geometric estimate of it. A tie tolerance sized on exact renders fails elsewhere: F10's 1e-3 held on the corpus symbol and failed on the first keystoned four-corner scene.

Benchmark delta: the image decode success path is unchanged within noise. `Image_Byte_Url_V6_M_Decode (Span)`, interleaved three times against `main` at 15 iterations, gave 33.65 / 33.42 / 33.33 µs on `main` against 33.45 / 34.52 / 31.21 µs here (the machine was loaded, and single ShortRun pairs swung ±3 µs). The noise failure path went 1,817 → 1,797 µs, 1,014 → 989, 2,007 → 2,170 and 1,553 → 1,584, noise-bound in both directions. The finder selection's worst case, 32 same-size candidates with no good triangle, is 41 µs with the second pass (21 µs after F10, 73 ns before). 4 to 8 candidates stay under 3 µs. The version read is 36 lookups and runs only on the failure path.

### One finder measurement for all three symbologies (2026-09-19)

Done. F12 lands on the same branch. Standard QR measured its module size in `QRImageDecoder` along the lines between its three finders, while Micro QR and rMQR, with one finder each, measured it in the shared `FinderAxisEstimator`, and F11 fixed only the first copy. Now there is one measurement:
- `FinderAxisEstimator.MeasureAxis` pairs edges of the same polarity, and `QRImageDecoder.MeasureBothWays` calls it instead of its own walk. The one behavioural difference, an outer ring that ends exactly at the image edge counting as complete, moved no Standard QR render in the three sweeps.
- `FindOrientationCandidates` fits the axis to the whole sweep first, and re-measures each candidate's size on off-center parallel rays.

The tests are `Decode_HalfPixelOffsetRender` for rMQR (10, 6 red before) and Micro QR (6, 1 red), `Decode_SupersampledRotatedRender` for both (4 and 6, 1 red each), and `FinderAxisEstimatorTest` (60 rotations of an M4 at 3 and 5 px/module, where the first candidate must lie within 1.5° of the axis and within 5 % of the module size, and 49 were red before). `SupersampledRenderer` moved to `tests/Shared` and takes any module grid, and `HalfPixelRenderer` joined it. The full suite passes: 21,905 tests, both target frameworks.

The measurement fix alone traded one failure for another, twice. Same-polarity pairing fixed every half-pixel render and gained 222 rMQR renders, but lost 68 clean Micro QR renders, all rotated. The cause was in the angular sweep, not the measurement.
- The size carried a selection bias. The sweep keeps the direction whose span is the smallest of 90, so the winning measurement is a low outlier, and a 17-module grid scaled from it misses its far modules. Re-measuring on four parallel rays offset ±0.5 and ±1 module (they cross the same ring edges at right angles inside the 3-module center square and took no part in the choice) brought rMQR to 1 loss, but Micro QR still lost 57.
- The direction was wrong. Near the axis the span grows only as 1/cos, a flat minimum that pixel noise moved 5-11° at 3 px/module (a 6.2° rotation offered 0°, 17°, 19°, 21°). The old 7-module measurement was coarse enough that many directions tied, and ties went to the lowest angles, 0°, 2°, 4°…, which covered small rotations by accident.

Fitting the square's span shape, 1/max(|cos|, |sin|), to all 180 measurements uses the sharp peaks toward the corners as well as the flat valley. It recovered those cases within about half a degree (6.8° for 6.2°, 5.2° for 5.0°, 13.2° for 12.7°, 11.2° for 10.8°). The old minima stay behind the fitted axis as candidates, so none was lost.

| Sweep, 8,000 renders each (flat, rotated, keystoned, both) | `main` | Branch | Gained | Lost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| rMQR, clean | 7,725 | 7,991 | 266 | 0 |
| rMQR, degraded | 6,632 | 7,109 | 488 | 11 |
| Micro QR, clean | 7,690 | 7,994 | 306 | 2 |
| Micro QR, degraded | 6,875 | 7,352 | 514 | 37 |

Every loss is at 3 to 4 px/module (the two clean Micro QR ones at 3 px/module with keystone), where each sweep gains several hundred.

Lessons. A shared component with a private copy gets fixed only once. F11 fixed Standard QR's copy of this walk, and the same asymmetry sat in the other copy until a different symbology hit it, so the measurement now lives in one place. Choosing by a minimum biases the value that did the choosing, so take the decision and the measurement from different samples. Noise decides the minimum of a function that is flat there, and an estimator that fits the whole curve uses the parts that are not flat. Again, a biased quantity had been supporting something downstream: the coarse measurement's ties had chosen small angles, and removing them exposed a direction estimate that had never worked on its own.

Benchmark delta, interleaved against `main` with two runs each at 10 iterations:

- `M4_ImageDecode_Span` 6.91 / 7.47 → 7.40 / 7.70 µs (+5 % on the mean, inside this machine's swing and the +10 % rule)
- `R7x43_ImageDecode_Span` 7.76 / 7.97 → 7.99 / 7.77 µs and `R17x139_ImageDecode_Span` 39.9 / 41.4 → 41.0 / 41.0 µs, flat
- `NoSymbol_Gradient_1144x168` 182 / 173 → 185 / 179 µs, flat
- `NoSymbol_Noise_1144x168` 8,782 / 8,374 → 6,593 / 6,626 µs (−23 %, both runs, and the cause was not investigated).

### Pixels are read by floor (2026-09-20)

Done. This is F13. The image decoders' coordinates put pixel edges on integers, and every place that turns a coordinate into a pixel now takes the floor:
- the Standard QR samplers (scalar, piecewise, both vector tiers), Micro QR's affine sampler, and rMQR's samplers (scalar, both vector tiers, format and timing reads, the sub-finder template)
- the alignment finder's ring checks, cross-check column and re-centring
- the finder-axis walk.

Two anchors that had carried the opposite half-pixel error are corrected with them. The alignment pattern's vertical centre was `+ 0.5` where the run's midpoint needs `+ 1`, and rMQR's sub-finder refinement walk rounded the same way the samplers did. `SymbolGeometry`'s note, which called the old rounding a harmless round-to-nearest, now says what it did.

`PixelConventionTest` has 25 cases, 24 red before (1 px/module and fractional builder sizes for all three symbologies, and the pixel-aligned sampler on both kernels). `Find_AxisAlignedPattern_CentreIsExact`, on both kernels, was red before. `QR_AlignmentPatternNotFound_CornersStayWithinAModuleAndAHalf` takes version 2 at ±2 % instead of +3 %. The full suite passes: 21,961 tests, both target frameworks.

In the clean sweep, pixel-aligned renders of every version × ECC × mask read from 2 px/module up, as did quiet zones 0 to 4 and right-angle rotations. Everything that failed was below about 2.2 px/module:

| Clean input | `main` | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Standard QR, 1 px/module | 0 / 2,560 | 2,560 / 2,560 |
| rMQR, 1 px/module | 4 / 256 | 256 / 256 |
| Micro QR, 1 px/module | 41 / 109 | 109 / 109 |
| Builder at fixed sizes, 1.5-2.2 px/module, all three | 288 / 676 | 666 / 676 |

The ten that remain are F14. Two of them read on `main` and not now (v23 at 244 px, R13x99 at 178 px), both in F14's band.

The half pixel had been helping by accident. On the F10-F12 sweeps the fix gained 70 and lost 54 clean Standard QR renders. The keystone-only losses were all version 1 at 3-8 % keystone, past its 2 % envelope. That sweep always shortens the top edge, so the finders-only fallback's bottom-right corner errs toward the bottom-right, the way the old offset pointed. With the keystone flipped, `main` drops from 19,871 to 19,721 while the fixed decoder reads 19,878 (+177 / −20, version 1 keystone +87 / −0). `main`'s corner test at version 2 and +3 % passed on the same luck: `main` fails it at +2.5 % and at −3 %, while the fixed decoder reads ±2 % alike (0.82 module at the corner either way), and version 10 with the alignment pattern erased reads ±0.75 % alike (0.83 module).

| Sweep against `main` | `main` | Now | Gained | Lost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Standard QR, clean (top edge shorter) | 19,871 | 19,887 | 70 | 54 |
| Standard QR, clean (bottom edge shorter) | 19,721 | 19,878 | 177 | 20 |
| Standard QR, degraded | 18,378 | 18,633 | 319 | 64 |
| rMQR, clean / degraded (8,000) | 7,991 / 7,109 | 7,997 / 7,196 | 6 / 96 | 0 / 9 |
| Micro QR, clean / degraded (8,000) | 7,994 / 7,352 | 7,999 / 7,406 | 5 / 76 | 0 / 22 |

Lessons. State a coordinate convention where the coordinates are consumed, not only where they are made: the finder code and `SymbolGeometry` both had it right, and every sampler ignored it. A bias harmless at the densities the tests use hides until the density drops. A half-pixel offset is invisible from 2.5 px/module up and a whole module at 1. A fix that removes a bias costs whatever the bias was supporting, here out-of-envelope keystone in one direction, and flipping the direction tells a real regression from lost luck.

Benchmark delta: unchanged within noise, interleaved against `main` with two runs each at 10 iterations: `Image_Byte_Url_V6_M_Decode (Span)` 32.40 / 31.80 → 32.12 / 31.97 µs, `M4_ImageDecode_Span` 7.21 / 7.18 → 7.15 / 7.22 µs, `R17x139_ImageDecode_Span` 39.61 / 39.57 → 39.23 / 39.49 µs.

### The timing pattern counts the version (2026-09-20)

Done. This is F14. `QRImageDecoder.CountTimingDimension` walks the timing row between the top-left and top-right finders and the timing column between the top-left and bottom-left ones, three modules in from their centres, and counts dark runs: 2v + 3 on either line. A line counts only if it starts and ends on a finder's dark edge row and every run between the finders is 0.4 to 1.6 modules long. The two lines must agree. When the estimate's sampling fails, the counted dimension is tried next, ahead of the version information and the runner-up.

`TimingPatternDimensionTest` has 136 cases:

- five fixed-size builder renders that read one or two versions off (v21 at 208 px as v22, v22 at 241 px as v24, and so on), all red before
- the count on pixel-aligned renders of every version at 1, 2 and 3 px/module, which must be exact
- seven rotated renders where the count may be 0 but never wrong
- a painted-over timing module in the row and in the column, where the count must refuse.

The full suite passes: 22,233 tests, both target frameworks.

The count first ran before the estimate and was moved. There it cost every successful decode two line walks: `Image_Byte_Url_V6_M_Decode (Span)` went from 32.08 to 34.89 µs on the mean of three interleaved runs, +8 %, paid on every image to help rare renders. Counted only after the estimate's sampling fails, with a quarter-module step instead of half a pixel, the success path is unchanged. The failing renders pay one extra sampling, which they needed anyway.

Standard QR now reads every render in F13's fixed-size probe (671 of 676 overall, and the 5 left are Micro QR and rMQR, F15) and 1,133 of 1,134 fixed-size builder renders across versions 1-40. The one left is v2 at 64 px, at the right version, also F15. The clean pixel-aligned sweep stays at 12,800 of 12,800. The rotated, keystoned and degraded sweeps are identical render for render (0 gained, 0 lost on each): on those inputs the estimate was already right wherever the count could read.

Lessons. A symbol that marks its own module positions beats any estimate of them, as the version information did for F11. The timing pattern is the cheaper of the two, readable at every version, and exact wherever each module is at least a pixel. A fallback's cost belongs on the failure path: the count is exact, but images that did not need it should not pay for it. Check what looks like one cause across three symbologies per decoder before writing it down: the Micro QR and rMQR renders in the same band were not dimension errors, because neither decoder estimates one.

Benchmark delta: unchanged, interleaved against the F13 commit with three runs each at 10 iterations: `Image_Byte_Url_V6_M_Decode` 32.74 / 32.55 / 32.14 → 32.33 / 32.53 / 32.10 µs, and `(Span)` 32.47 / 31.80 / 32.73 → 32.08 / 32.64 / 33.73 µs.

### The finders are the fallback for a coarse alignment anchor (2026-09-20)

Done. This is F15, for Standard QR. `BuildGridTransform` now reports whether it anchored on the alignment pattern, and the parallelogram of the three finder centres is its own method, `BuildParallelogramTransform`. When the alignment-anchored global sampling fails to decode, `SampleAndDecode` resamples once through the parallelogram before giving up. Corners follow whichever transform decoded.

`Decode_LowDensityFlatRender_AlignmentCentreTooCoarse_FallsBackToTheFinders` covers four fixed-size builder renders at level L (v2 at 64 and 68 px, v3 at 61 px), all red before. The full suite passes: 22,241 tests, both target frameworks.

One diagnostic run showed the row's first hypothesis wrong. F15 was filed blaming modules the builder draws 1 px wide, but Skia fills a non-antialiased rectangle's pixel when the pixel's centre lies inside it, so flooring a true module centre always lands inside the module, however narrow. Sampling the failing renders through the decoder's own transform and comparing with the matrix put every wrong module (17 to 22 per render) in the bottom-right block. The finder centres were within 0.14 px, and every column and row along the timing lines sampled correctly. The alignment centre was 0.36 px off (44.00 against 43.64), a pixel-resolved midpoint of a 1-2 px run, and the four-point transform read it as perspective. The parallelogram of the finders alone sampled the same renders with 0 wrong modules.

Of 9,600 fixed-size builder renders of versions 1-6 at 1.5-2.5 px/module, 31 failed and 0 fail now. Standard QR's fixed-size renders across versions 1-40 read 1,134 of 1,134, and the clean pixel-aligned sweep stays at 12,800 of 12,800. Both clean rotation/keystone sweeps are unchanged render for render. The degraded sweep gains 24 and loses none (18,633 → 18,657).

Lessons. Measure before designing the fix a hypothesis implies: the fix F15 was filed with (read each column's pixels off the timing pattern) targeted a cause that was not there, and one diagnostic run replaced it with a fallback of a few lines. An anchor is only as good as its resolution relative to how far the transform extrapolates from it: the alignment pattern sits 6.5 modules from the corner, the finders 3.5, and at 2 px/module a centre resolved to a pixel is a third of a module. A fallback that replaces only failures, never successes, cannot regress what already read. This one keeps keystoned symbols on the alignment anchor.

Benchmark delta: unchanged, interleaved against the F14 commit with two runs each at 10 iterations: `Image_Byte_Url_V6_M_Decode` 32.01 / 32.24 → 33.39 / 32.40 µs, and `(Span)` 32.08 / 32.67 → 31.92 / 32.25 µs. The fallback runs only after a failed decode.

### Micro QR measures its frame on the timing patterns (2026-09-20)

Done. This is F16. `MicroQRImageDecoder.TryTimingFrame` measures the grid on row 0 and column 0, the timing patterns that run from the finder to the symbol's far edge. `TryFitTimingLine` walks each line back to the finder's outer edge and forward across the separator and the timing modules to the quiet zone, recording every module boundary, and fits position = start + pitch · index by least squares. The two fits give the symbol's corner and a pitch per axis, and the dark runs give the size, on which both lines must agree. A line that does not read as a timing pattern is refused: a run outside 0.4-1.6 modules, a size outside 11-17, or a pitch outside 0.7-1.4 of the finder's. The axis-aligned fast path tries this frame once per orientation after every finder-scaled size has failed.

`MicroQRTimingFrameTest` had 92 cases at the time (118 after the review rounds below): M3 at 37 px and M4 at 41 px, both red before, and every builder size of M2-M4 from 1.5 to 3 px/module in all four right-angle rotations, where M3 at 39 px was also red. The full suite passes: 22,425 tests, both target frameworks.

A fit beats the two ends. Each boundary the walk finds is quantized to about half a pixel, and at 1.95 px/module a sample has only 0.47 px of margin. A pitch from the finder's outer edge and the far edge alone would carry both ends' quantization into every module. The fit spreads it over the 7 to 12 boundaries a line crosses. The failing renders had the finder at 2.000 px/module against a true 1.947 and its centre 0.29 px off, which put the far modules 0.7-1 px out.

Micro QR now reads every render in F13's fixed-size probe and in the library's builder sweep (374 of 374), and every clean pixel-aligned render (545 of 545). On the rotated and keystoned sweeps it is unchanged on clean renders and gains 1 degraded render, losing none. F13's probe now fails only rMQR's three renders, F17.

Lessons. A single-finder symbology extrapolates whatever its finder measures across the whole symbol, so any error in the finder's scale grows with the symbol's size. The timing patterns reach the far edge and remove the extrapolation instead of refining it. A measurement built from quantized boundaries should use all of them, not the two furthest apart.

Benchmark delta: unchanged. `M4_ImageDecode_Span`, interleaved against the F15 commit with two runs each at 10 iterations, went 7.17 / 7.16 → 7.19 / 7.33 µs. Micro QR decoding of salt-and-pepper noise images (the failure path, where the fallback is tried for every orientation of up to eight candidates) went 20,439 / 20,490 → 19,702 / 20,028 µs at 256 px, 14,069 / 14,024 → 13,638 / 13,847 µs and 37,702 / 37,877 → 35,319 / 35,485 µs at 512 px, and 13,064 / 13,500 → 12,841 / 13,928 µs at 1,024 px. The timing lines refuse noise on their first runs.

### rMQR searches the finder scale for its format read (2026-09-20)

Done. This is F17. `RmQRImageDecoder` reads the finder-side format copy through the finder's local frame, as before. When the copy does not read at the measured scale, it now tries `FormatReadScales` (±2, ±4, ±6 and ±8 %, nearest first) and keeps the first scale that reads, for the sub-finder search and every frame after it. The review rounds below replaced that: the search continues while the frames fail, under a bound on the finder's measured module. A read at a corrected scale counts only if it is an exact codeword.

`RmQRFormatScaleTest` had 165 cases at the time (174 after the review rounds below): the three renders F13's probe left, and builder sizes from 1.5 to 2.5 px/module for five versions, every third pixel. Four renders were red before (the three, and R17x139 at 247 px). The full suite passes: 22,755 tests, both target frameworks.

Measurement cleared the suspect. F17 was filed suspecting the sub-finder, F15's mechanism on rMQR's far anchor. On the failing renders the sub-finder was located within 0.5 px, and the anisotropic frame it gives sampled R13x99 and R15x99 with 0 wrong modules. A frame at the true pitch from the measured finder centre sampled all four renders with 0 wrong modules. The symbol was lost earlier. The version comes from the finder-side format copy at columns 8-11, read through the finder's frame, and the finder measured 1.833 against a true 1.728 px/module (+6 %). At column 11 that is 0.8 px, so the copy did not read and the decoder returned. At ×0.97 the copy read the right version on every failing render.

Exactness keeps the search cheap. The first version accepted any read within 3 bits, as the unscaled read does, and the no-symbol noise benchmark went from 7.4 to 21.0 ms. With 64 finder-side words of 18 bits, a random read lands within 3 bits of one about a quarter of the time, so nine tries per frame almost always produced a version, and a false version paid for the sub-finder and perspective searches behind it. ×1.06 even read R11x77 as R17x77 on a real render. Requiring an exact codeword at the corrected scales brings a random match to about 0.02 % per try. The clean renders read exactly at the right scale.

F13's fixed-size probe now reads 676 of 676 across the three symbologies. rMQR's builder sweep reads 732 of 732 and the clean pixel-aligned sweep 1,280 of 1,280. The rotated and keystoned sweeps are identical to F13, clean and degraded.

Lessons. A bounded search validated by a checksum is a fair repair, but the checksum's tolerance must shrink with the number of tries: a safe acceptance rule for one read is a near-certain false positive over nine. When the pipeline has an early exit, look there first. Everything downstream of the format read was already right.

Benchmark delta, interleaved against the F16 commit with two runs each at 10 iterations:

- `R7x43_ImageDecode_Span` 7.66 / 7.54 → 7.73 / 7.61 µs and `R17x139_ImageDecode_Span` 40.59 / 39.76 → 39.65 / 39.72 µs, flat
- `NoSymbol_Gradient_1144x168` 182 / 179 → 184 / 180 µs, flat
- `NoSymbol_Noise_1144x168` 7,588 / 7,367 → 7,694 / 7,692 µs, +2.5 % (21,048 / 21,053 µs before the exact-codeword rule).

The clean-image series (F13-F17) is complete. Every render in F13's probe of fixed-size builder output at 1.5-2.2 px/module now reads, in all three symbologies, as does every clean pixel-aligned render from 1 px/module up. Five causes lay behind "clean images that do not read":
- a half-pixel sampling convention (F13)
- a dimension estimate thrown off by whole-pixel snapping, fixed by counting the timing pattern (F14)
- an alignment anchor too coarse at 2 px/module, with the finders as the fallback (F15)
- Micro QR's finder scale extrapolated across the symbol, replaced by a timing-pattern fit (F16)
- rMQR's format read at the finder's scale, which now searches nearby scales (F17).

### An estimate past version 40 is counted, not refused (2026-09-20)

Done. The F18 sweep found this, and it was fixed on the same branch because it is F14's count failing to run. `TryEstimateDimension` clamps the estimate to versions 1-40 and refuses it when it lies more than four modules from the snapped dimension. At versions 39 and 40 the builder's whole-pixel snapping makes the finders measure a few percent small (2.857 px/module against a true 2.918 on v40 at 540 px), which puts a 177-module symbol past 181, so the decoder returned `NotDetected` before the timing count could run. On every failing render the count read 177 (173 for v39). `DecodeLuminanceCore` now counts when the estimate is refused, and samples at the count if both lines agree. With no count it stays `NotDetected`. The count is taken once either way.

`TimingPatternDimensionTest` gains 9 cases per framework: seven builder renders (v39 at 350 and 385 px, v40 at 285, 320, 358, 443 and 540 px), all red before, and two negative classes that were already `NotDetected` and must stay so. These are the v40 render at 540 px with four light timing modules painted over, where nothing counts, and three finders with two timing lines drawn as a version 45 symbol would draw them, where the count is exact but names no version. The full suite passes: 22,773 tests (374 skipped on this x64 machine: the AdvSimd kernels), both target frameworks.

Builder renders of Standard QR versions 1-40 at all four levels, at every size from 1.5 to 3 px/module, failed 218 times before (v40 at 48 sizes per level, v39 at 6) and 2 times after (v19-H at 195 px and v27-L at 255 px, `DataUncorrectable`, filed under F18).

Lessons. A sanity check placed in front of a fallback decides whether the fallback ever runs. F14 put the count after the estimate's sampling, which was right for cost, but the estimate could fail before sampling, and that early exit skipped it. The sweeps behind F13-F17 missed this because they probed a sample of sizes, not every size. At v40 the failing sizes come in bands a few pixels wide. A sweep that compares two builds case by case needs seeds that are the same in both processes: `string.GetHashCode` and `HashCode.Combine` are randomized per process, so seeding from them compared two different samples.

Benchmark delta: unchanged against the F17 commit at 10 iterations: `Image_Byte_Url_V6_M_Decode` 32.91 → 32.01 µs and `(Span)` 31.93 → 32.06 µs. The change runs only after the estimate is refused.

### Adversarial review of the clean-image branch (2026-09-20)

Done. Three reviewers (one on Standard QR, one on Micro QR and rMQR, one on tests, docs and API) raised 12 claims, and three verifiers tried to refute each. None was refuted. Three concerned behaviour, and nine coverage and docs.

- rMQR stopped its scale search at the first scale whose copy read. Which finder modules the snapping widens depends on the orientation, so R11x77 at 137 px, the render F17 names, read its copy exactly at the measured scale when turned 270°, 3.5 % off, and the frame built on it failed. R13x99 at 211 px did the same at 180° and 270° with the sub-finder found. `TryFrame` now moves to the next scale while frames fail (the frame body is `TryScaledFrame`). A corrected scale must still read an exact codeword.
- The same search slowed rMQR's failures on other symbologies' images, 2× on a Micro QR image, because every frame whose copy did not read tried eight more scales. The search stopped at a finder module of 3 px, on the argument that snapping moves the finder's measured size by about a pixel over its 6-module span, about 1.3 px at column 11 at any density, which the half-module margin covers from 3 px/module up. The fourth round below measured that wrong, and the cutoff is 6 px.
- F15's finder fallback made Standard QR's finder-found failures 15-40 % slower (F15's fallback alone, damaged data, v2 to v40 at 2-4 px/module). The failure-path figures below compare the whole pre-review branch against `main`, so their spread is wider. Instrumentation put all the cost in two places where the resample cannot help: at the true size a flat symbol samples identically through both anchors, and at the runner-up the grid is the wrong size either way. The resample is now compared with the first sampling and decoded only if it differs, and `SampleAndDecode` takes no fallback for the runner-up.
- Coverage: corners were never asserted on the new success paths (the finder fallback, the Micro QR timing frame including its mirrored branch, the timing-count decodes). The timing-line refusals, rMQR's exact-codeword rule and the refused estimate's status had no negative test. Two floor sites were unguarded. M1 was missing from the timing-frame sweep and v10 from the corner test whose figure the spec quotes. Docs: a test comment said the count goes first, and `SymbolFitsImage`'s summary had been left on `TryTimingFrame`.

The round added these tests. `DrawnCorners` (corners read off an axis-aligned render's dark pixels, tolerance in modules) checks the finder-fallback, Micro QR timing-frame and timing-count decodes, plus a mirrored timing-frame case. The finder-fallback and timing-frame ones fail with the corner transform or the transposed flag swapped, the timing-count ones with the flag only (on a flat render their mesh and global transforms agree). `MicroQRTimingLineTest` has 11 cases: sizes 11-17 read, the image edge ends a line, and a line longer than M4 (which also keeps the frame inside the 17 × 17 buffer), a run of three modules, a pitch 0.65 of the finder's, a light start and an over-long finder run are each refused. Each refusal fails with its own guard removed. `Decode_FinderBesideRandomFormatBits_IsNotDetected` uses four seeds that read within 1-3 bits only at a corrected scale and turn `DataUncorrectable` with the rule loosened. `Decode_EstimatePastVersion40_DataDestroyed_ReportsTheDataFailure` is new, as are `Find_LowDensity_CentreIsExact` (alignment ring and cross-check column at 1 and 2 px/module) and `DarkLightDarkRun_PixelAlignedFinder_FindsTheRingEdges` (one walk direction: the module size pairs a forward walk with a backward one, so a half-pixel probe cancels there). The rMQR fixed-size and fractional tests now run all four right angles and were red before on R11x77 at 137 px and R13x99 at 211 px. The full suite passed after every round: 22,885 tests in Debug and 22,903 in Release (374 skipped on this x64 machine: the AdvSimd kernels), both target frameworks.

`RecenterX`'s floor is unchanged: a half-pixel probe there lands in the same dark run or on a light pixel that leaves the row hit as it was, so only a contrived input tells the two apart. The refused estimate's low end (below 17 modules) needs a finder measured about 40 % large and has no test.

A second round on these fixes raised six claims, none refuted. The continued scale search made a damaged rMQR symbol below 3 px/module fail 3-5.3× slower (R17x139 at 2 px/module: 24 → 126 ms), because the copy reads exactly at most scales and each reran the sub-finder, affine and perspective frames. The third round below has the fix. The rest concerned tests and docs:

- the light-start refusal case was refused by the finder-run minimum, not its own guard, and now puts one light pixel under the start of an otherwise valid line
- F18(b) had no upright case, and R11x77 at 140 px now fails upright when the search stops at the first scale that reads
- the scale cutoff had no functional test (the fourth and fifth rounds below add one at 7 and at 5.1 px/module)
- the timing-count corner claim, the F17 row and the rMQR spec still described the first-read rule.

The identical-sampling skip and the runner-up exclusion still have no functional test, because they can only skip work.

A third round found the second round's fix unsound. It had `TryScaledFrame` reuse an earlier scale's result when the sub-finder landed within half a pixel of the earlier one, on the argument that the refined frames are built on the sub-finder. The sub-finder moves 0.2-0.4 px between scales, so the tolerance paired failed results with anchors that had moved, and the perspective search is not built on the sub-finder alone, because it takes its row pitch from the starting scale. On a sweep of 1,920 mildly warped renders at 1.6-2.9 px/module, the reuse read 735 where rerunning every scale read 782 (the branch before this review: 661). Two stop rules were measured instead. Stopping after any frame that reads format information lost the test file's own renders, because a frame built on a wrong scale also fails in the data, as a damaged symbol does. The shipped rule stops after frames anchored on the sub-finder read format information and continues while there is no sub-finder: every test case reads, 739 of the 1,920 warped renders read, the rotation and fixed-size sweeps stay complete (24,304 of 24,304 and 32,400 of 32,400), and damaged symbols whose sub-finder is intact fail within 4 % of the branch before this review (the fourth round below covers a hidden sub-finder). Recovering the 43 warped renders it gives up against rerunning every scale needs the perspective search to search its own row pitch. That is F18. Two comments were also corrected: the fractional-size test cited a render it never draws, and the F18 row still read as if (b) were open.

A fourth round found the 3 px cutoff on the scale search wrong in both directions. Its argument (a half-module margin covers the snapping error from 3 px up) has no slack in its own numbers, about 1.3 px against 1.5, and measurement contradicted it: clean non-square and mildly warped renders at 3-4.2 px/module read only at a corrected scale, and the cutoff lost eight of them against the branch before this review. The cutoff is now 6 px/module, a measured bound, which loses nothing against that branch and keeps the whole speedup on other symbologies' images (lifting it entirely would read more still, which is F18(g)). The round also measured what the continued search costs a damaged symbol whose sub-finder is hidden: 2-3×, because every scale that reads the copy searches for the sub-finder again. Restricting the scales to ±4 % barely moved that cost, and skipping an unrefined frame whose format information an earlier scale had already read looked like the saving (the fifth round shows it was neither a saving nor sound), so the cost stands and F18(f) records it. The review chose to keep those reads: a symbol whose sub-finder is hidden is damaged, and this branch is about clean images.

A fifth round found the fourth round's other change, skipping an unrefined frame whose format information an earlier scale had already read, both wrong and pointless. At a corrected scale that frame is a different grid: the format copy is within 11 modules of the finder and still reads a few percent off, while the far data is several modules out, so the corrected scale is the one that decodes. On clean renders whose sub-finder is painted out, the skip cost 1,664 correct decodes of 5,704 (the 1,426 renders above in their four right angles, none gained), and on exactly those renders it was 11-23× slower, because a success ends the scale loop and a skip cannot. It is removed: the unrefined frame runs at every scale, which reads 1,166 of 1,426 such renders against 814 for the branch before this review, and damaged symbols are unchanged. The class is wider than "hidden": the sub-finder template accepts 24 of 25 samples, so two wrong modules in that corner put a render in it, and a review sweep put 12 % of otherwise pristine low-density renders there. The round also found the scale loop missing the attempt-budget guard its siblings have (unreachable at the shipped budget of 256, found by forcing it to 3) and the cutoff untested from below, which `Decode_SubFinderPaintedOut_ReadsAtACorrectedScale` now checks at 5.1 and 4.9 px/module, red at the old 3. Four doc statements were corrected with it: the skip described as a free saving in two places, a superseded 3 px bullet left in the present tense, a test that no longer exists, and one duplicated benchmark pair.

rMQR builder renders of every version at every width from 1.5 to 3 px/module, four contents and two levels, read 32,400 of 32,400, where F18(b) had 41 failing. Every version from 1.5 to 6 px/module in four rotations reads 24,304 of 24,304 (the branch before this review: 24,290). Standard QR builder renders of v1-40 at four levels from 1.5 to 3 px/module read 25,758 of 25,760 before and after, the two being F18(d). The failure-path cost (fastest of five interleaved runs) was: damaged Standard QR v2 at 4 px 75 → 81 µs against `main` (the branch before this review: 100), v6 at 2 px 139 → 85 (139), v10 at 4 px 210 → 229 (324), v25 at 3 px 1,508 → 1,544 (1,936), v40 at 3 px 2,807 → 3,027 (3,192). rMQR decoding a Micro QR image at 200 px went 580 → 284 µs and a Standard QR image at 400 px 2,407 → 1,495 µs against the branch before this review.

Lessons. Measure a failure-path cost on failures: every delta F15 and F17 recorded was the success path or the no-symbol path, and the costs were on symbols that are found and do not read. A search that stops at the first acceptable answer assumes that answer is right. A checksum that passes at a wrong scale is still a wrong scale, so the search must continue on the frame's outcome, not the read's. When measuring a fallback's extra work, count where it runs before tuning what it does: here all of it was on attempts where it could not change the result. The second round found the same in the first round's own fix: a search told to continue must not redo work that does not depend on what it searches. The third round found that fix's premise wrong: "this does not depend on the scale" must be checked against every consumer of the scale, and one of them, the perspective search's row pitch, did depend on it.

Benchmark delta: the success and no-symbol paths are unchanged against the branch before this review, at 10 iterations: `Image_Byte_Url_V6_M_Decode` 34.69 → 32.20 µs, `(Span)` 35.83 → 32.99 µs, `R7x43_ImageDecode_Span` 7.45 → 7.51 µs, `R17x139_ImageDecode_Span` 39.24 → 38.83 µs, `NoSymbol_Noise_1144x168` 7,556 → 7,673 µs, `NoSymbol_Gradient_1144x168` 174 → 176 µs.

### A poor triple with candidates left out sends the scan over the skipped rows (2026-09-20)

Done. This is F18(d), for Standard QR. `TrySelectBestThree` reports when it dropped candidates seen on one row and the triple it chose without them scores past 0.25 (`DoubtfulTripleScore`). The score is the selection's own, skew plus module-size spread. `TryFindCore` answers that as it answers a failed selection, with the complementary rescan, and takes the full sweep's triple when it is confirmed over at least as much height as the stride's. The selection rule itself is unchanged, and so is every image whose stride triple is not doubtful.

`FinderPatternSelectionTest` gains 12 cases per framework:

- two builder renders red before (v19-H at 195 px, v34-M at 312 px)
- four keystoned renders that must keep the stride's triple, one of them red with the height rule removed
- the flag's classes, namely the measured shape in every scan order, four confirmed candidates holding no triple, the bound from both sides (0.24 not flagged, 0.33 flagged), and a poor triple with nothing left out, confirmed or not.

The full suite passes: 23,615 tests (374 skipped on this x64 machine), both target frameworks.

The row guessed sampling. The cause was selection. F18(d) was filed as `DataUncorrectable` and "not diagnosed". Sampled through the decoder's own transforms, the v19-H render had 3,655 wrong modules of 8,649, and the bottom-left "finder" was at (28, 165) with a module size of 3.43 against a true (14.7, 180.3) and 1.92. The real finder was in the candidate list. At 1.9 px/module its 3-module band is 5 rows, the stride is 3, and the scan hit it once, while a false candidate in the data was hit twice. `Count >= 2` then compacted the list to exactly three, and three candidates return before any scoring, so the rescan that exists for this never ran. The failures depend on content: with four short contents, 3 of 103,040 builder renders (v1-40, four levels, every size from 1.5 to 3 px/module) failed, all this class. v27-L at 255 px did not fail with them.

Several shapes were measured before this one. Scoring every candidate, confirmed or not, fixed the renders and broke the tested rule that a once-seen candidate does not displace a confirmed triple. Scoring them only when the confirmed triple is poor kept that rule and lost 9 of 4,000 renders under keystone up to 20 %: a real triple under keystone scores well past 0.25 (median 0.29 at up to 20 %, 0.88 at most, against 0.11 flat), so "poor" fired on real triples and let a once-seen false candidate in. Rescanning and selecting again lost 3, because the rows that confirm the real finders also confirm a false candidate at the symbol's centre, which closes a right isosceles triangle over one side of the symbol. Keeping the stride's triple unless the sweep's is confirmed on as many rows lost the two F18 renders again, because a false candidate of twice the module size is confirmed on as many rows as a real finder. Rows divided by module size ships. One more rule, that the sweep's triple must itself score under the bound, changed no render in any sweep once the height rule was in, and was deleted.

Builder renders as above went from 103,037 to 103,040 of 103,040. Supersampled renders at 2-6 px/module, any rotation, 4,000 per symbology with keystone up to 20 %, are identical render for render (3,387 Standard QR). 6,000 with keystone up to 6 % show +1 / −0. Micro QR and rMQR do not go through this path and are identical in both.

Lessons. A status names where the decode gave up, not where it went wrong: a wrong finder triple surfaces as `DataUncorrectable`. A count taken under a stride is an undercount, and a rule that trusts it (`Count >= 2`) needs the full sweep before it can overrule geometry. A bound sized on flat renders says nothing about keystoned ones. The score distribution had to be measured per keystone before 0.25 meant anything, and it means only "worth a sweep". A guard that no sweep and no test can tell from its absence is not a guard.

Benchmark delta: unchanged against `main` at 10 iterations: `Image_Byte_Url_V6_M_Decode` 31.81 → 30.96 µs, `(Span)` 30.91 → 30.95 µs. Only a doubtful stride triple pays for the rescan: 300 supersampled decodes with keystone up to 20 % took 76.0 → 77.4 ms (+1.8 %), and the flat set is unchanged (65.3 → 65.5 ms).

### A near miss of the finder ratio is measured again from grey levels (2026-09-20)

Done. This is F18(a), for all three symbologies. `Binarizer.ComputeOtsuThreshold` also returns `GreyLevels`, the luminance of a wholly dark and a wholly light pixel, from the histogram it already has (the mean of each class's outer half). `FinderPatternFinder` takes them, and wherever it checks 1:1:3:1:1 (the row scan, scalar and vector, and the vertical, horizontal and diagonal cross-checks), runs that fail by no more than 1.5 px are measured again: each of the six edges moves off its pixel boundary by the coverage of the pixel on either side, and the five widths are held to the same half-module tolerance. With no pixel strictly between the two levels the measurement could only repeat the whole-pixel runs, so `GreyLevels` comes back disabled and the scan is the old one. From 3 px/module the strict tolerance is 1.5 px or more, so a finder there is never a near miss.

`AntiAliasedEdgeDecodeTest` has 144 cases per framework (one anti-aliased path render per symbology at 2.0-2.5 px/module and eight sub-pixel offsets), 38 red before. Each case first asserts which edges it rendered: grey for all but the whole scale at the whole offset, which lands every edge on a pixel boundary and is the class's crisp decode, one per symbology. `FinderRatioCoverageTest` has 21 cases:

- a lone finder found only by coverage, with its centre
- concentric squares 2:1:3:1:2 that the second look must refuse, four reaching it in the row scan and two in the vertical cross-check after their rows pass the whole-pixel ratio (the review round instrumented this: the near-miss tolerance turns all six away before any coverage arithmetic runs, so the earlier reading, that the measurement refuses them and that a mutant accepting every measurement makes all six candidates, was wrong on both counts, and the diagonal is never reached on this fixture)
- two-level noise at 1-2 px scanned candidate for candidate as before
- no candidate appearing, moving or gaining a row at 3-4.5 px/module
- scalar and vector scans agreeing on anti-aliased renders
- `GreyLevels` disabled for two levels, one class and low contrast.

`AntiAliasedRenderer` is the shared test renderer. The full suite passes: 23,963 tests (374 skipped on this x64 machine), both target frameworks.

Two alternatives were measured first, because the row asked for the false-candidate rate as well. A tolerance floor of 1.5 px, close to what zxing-cpp does (half a module plus half a pixel), reads the same renders but takes the candidate list on 1 px two-level noise from 5 to the cap of 32, making the single-finder failure paths 2-4x slower. Retrying a failed image upscaled 2x bilinearly reads a little more than what ships (anti-aliased Standard QR at 1.5-2 px/module 299 of 300 against 281, Micro QR builder shapes 594 of 600 against 559), because it repairs the sampling as well as the finders, but costs every unreadable image 2.5-18x (no-symbol noise 5.1 to 12.6 ms, a damaged v40 at 3 px/module 2.2 to 16.8 ms) and four times its pixels in a rented buffer. Its advantage is the sampling, which can be added later on the symbol's own area once the finders are known.

Measured with 300 renders per cell against `main`, anti-aliased path renders at 1.5-2 / 2-2.5 px/module went Standard QR 225 → 281 / 227 → 300, Micro QR 254 → 291 / 229 → 300, rMQR 263 → 300 / 229 → 300. Builder finder shapes went Standard QR 143 → 285 / 199 → 300 (and 287 → 300 at 2.5-3.5), Micro QR 189 → 284 / 230 → 275, rMQR 170 → 294 / 207 → 300. A 1 px/module image upscaled bilinearly went Standard QR 144 → 226 / 159 → 289, Micro QR 150 → 229 / 120 → 283, rMQR 162 → 291 / 94 → 300. Crisp renders read 300 of 300 in every cell, before and after. Supersampled renders at 2-6 px/module, any rotation, a third of them keystoned, 3,000 per symbology, gained +191 / +93 / +110 and lost none. An inward margin on the two levels (a sixteenth of the range, against noise on flat modules) cost 11 builder-shape renders and was dropped.

Lessons. When a check fails on a measurement artefact, repair the measurement and keep the check: the tolerance keeps data runs out of the candidate list, and every version that loosened it paid in candidates. A second look that provably equals the first on some class of input should be switched off for that class by that proof, not by a heuristic: "no pixel between the levels" costs nothing on two-level images and cannot change a result, whereas a grey-mass threshold of 1 % lost the builder's finder-shape renders, whose only grey pixels are the finders'. Measure where the time goes before cutting it: early rejection inside the measurement and an integer near-miss test changed nothing, because with the measurement stubbed out 75 % of the added cost remained, in the near-miss branch on every window.

Benchmark delta: within noise against `main` at 10 iterations: `Image_Byte_Url_V6_M_Decode` 33.19 → 32.16 µs, `(Span)` 33.14 → 34.37 µs, `M4_ImageDecode_Span` 8.98 → 7.58 µs, `R7x43_ImageDecode_Span` 7.89 → 8.17 µs, `R17x139_ImageDecode_Span` 40.63 → 41.63 µs, `NoSymbol_Noise_1144x168` 7,935 → 8,037 µs, `NoSymbol_Gradient_1144x168` 183.8 → 185.9 µs. On the failure paths (fastest of seven at 512 px), two-level noise and damaged crisp symbols are unchanged (Standard QR 5.10 → 5.22 ms on 1 px noise, damaged v40 at 3 px/module 2.17 → 2.18 ms). Blurred 1 px noise, where every window is a near miss with grey in it, went 1.13 → 2.09 ms for Standard QR and 1.34 → 2.54 ms for Micro QR and rMQR, and blurred 2 px noise at 30 % density went 34.8 → 48.3 ms for Micro QR (not broken down further).

### Adversarial review of the grey-level branch (2026-09-20)

Done. Five rounds of parallel review covered the branch, then three independent verifiers checked each shortlisted claim. Two claims were refuted and dropped, one of them by all three (it said the branch's negative coverage was tautological, but two tests do run the loosened path on non-symbol content).

The important finding is a false accept caused by the near-miss gate mixing two kinds of tolerance. The strict check's tolerance is relative, half a module per module, so the three-module centre run gets three times the outer runs'. The near-miss tolerance is absolute, standing for edge pixels landing on the wrong side of the threshold, and a run has two edges however wide it is. Tripling it for the centre made a run of five equal modules a near miss. As a result, a cross whose middle row and column read 1:1:3:1:1 and whose diagonal reads 1:1:1:1:1 became a candidate, a shape the whole-pixel scan refuses at every render offset tried. Three verifiers reproduced it independently (74, 281 and 1,210 accepting windows over their own sweeps, all attributed to the diagonal by holding the other stages on whole pixels), and on 300 random grids with three planted finders the candidates sitting on no finder went 11 → 18/20. The centre budget is now the outer one.

The round also shipped two changes. The near test is an unsigned range test, because `Math.Abs(int)` must branch for `int.MinValue`, and this part of the second look runs on every window. The grey levels became a required parameter, because the default was "feature off" and two pre-existing suites were silently testing only the unchanged path through it.

Swept at every density from 2.0 to 4.0 with 256 sub-pixel offsets each, the false accept is refused from 2.25 px/module up and still admitted below that, the second look's remaining hole: the coverage measurement crosses module corners, where a pixel's darkness is not one edge's position, so the runs it measures there can pass the ratio. From 2.05 px/module up the route is the two axis cross-checks, not the diagonal, so measuring the diagonal on whole pixels changes nothing there. Below that the route is the diagonal, and holding it to whole pixels costs 19 of the anti-aliased renders their decode. The repair is the corner model. Against the branch before the review, `NoSymbol_Noise_1144x168` went 8,037 → 7,970 µs and `NoSymbol_Gradient_1144x168` 185.9 → 185.0 µs, both back near `main`'s 7,935 and 183.8 because a tighter gate measures fewer windows. `M4_ImageDecode_Span` 8.2 µs, `R7x43_ImageDecode_Span` 9.3 µs and `R17x139_ImageDecode_Span` 45.3 µs are inside this box's spread, which is too wide to resolve a few percent. The near test's own kernel, measured in isolation against a byte-identical canary, is 6-12 % faster on blurred noise, about 28 % of what the branch had added there. The full suite runs 23,975 tests, 0 failed, both frameworks.

Lessons. An absolute tolerance and a relative one do not compose: scaling a pixel-sized allowance by a run's width in modules lets a wider run be more wrong, the opposite of what an edge artefact does, and the scaling admits exactly the window that is not 1:1:3:1:1. A second look can only loosen a rejection filter reached after everything else accepted, so the test that matters measures its refusals: across every anti-aliased fixture in the suite, the diagonal's coverage check had 61 accepts and 0 refusals, and nothing tested the half of its contract that does the work. A trailing optional parameter whose default turns a fix off is a trap: the two suites that guard the scan's critical invariants kept compiling and silently stopped covering the path under review.

### A crisp symbol under 1.5 px/module is read through its module boundaries (2026-09-21)

Done. This is F18(c), for all three symbologies. The user made the decision the row asked for: in the envelope. Two changes read edges where the decoders measured sizes. In the finder (`FinderPatternFinder`), a window whose runs have the shape a small crisp finder leaves (four runs of 1 or 2 px around one of 3 to 5) and that a neighbouring row repeats pixel for pixel goes to the cross-checks. Where the ratio cross-checks refuse it, `TryCrossCheckWholePattern` takes the runs of the row and the column through the centre and reads all 49 modules through those six edges. For the grid, the new shared `ModuleBoundaryReader` builds a table of the module boundaries along each axis from a timing line (every boundary past the finder), the finders' centre lines (boundaries 1, 2, 5, 6 of their own seven), and, for the two inside a three-module run, the positions where the modules in line with it change colour. A least-squares fit fills only what nothing crossed. Each module is read at the middle pixel of its cell. Standard QR reads module row 6 and column 6 from finder to finder (both must count the same valid dimension). Micro QR and rMQR read row 0 and column 0 from the finder's edge rows to the quiet zone, with rMQR allowing the three-module alignment and corner runs that sit on its timing rows and requiring the counted size to be a version's. The table is used below 1.75 px/module at the finder, on symbols along the image axes, before the fitted grids in Standard QR and rMQR and after them in Micro QR.

`FractionalLowDensityDecodeTest` has 172 cases per framework, every builder size from 1 to 1.5 px/module for Standard QR v1/3/7/10, Micro QR M2-M4 and four rMQR versions, with drawn corners. 95 were red before. `ModuleBoundaryReaderTest` has 115:

- nearest-neighbour renders at four densities in all four right angles, mirrored and not, per symbology
- a painted timing module in the row or the column refusing the table (with the unpainted render as control)
- finders off the image axes refusing it
- timing lines ending at the quiet zone, on a finder, with a three-module run allowed and refused, and three lines that are not timing lines
- boundary fill between neighbours and its refusal
- the two inner boundaries read from two edges and left open on one, none or three.

`FinderWholePatternTest` has 37:

- a lone crisp finder at five densities and four offsets (6 of the 20 need the new path)
- a finder with one ring module dark, refused at 1.25 px/module (6 of 7 become candidates under a mutant whose whole-pattern check always matches)
- 10 two-level noise images held to the candidate counts of the scan without the new path.

The full suite passes: 24,605 tests (374 skipped on this x64 machine), both target frameworks.

Several things were tried on the way. A least-squares grid through the timing boundaries (the Micro QR timing frame's method) read Standard QR crisp renders 136 → 268 of 300 at 1.0-1.25 px/module and stopped there: a fit good to a tenth of a pixel is not enough when the margin is (pitch − 1) / 2. The table, which needs no margin, read 297, and reading the finders' inner boundaries from the data instead of fitting them read 300. The first near-miss gate (the 1.5 px absolute tolerance of the grey second look, under 12 px) cost 1 px noise +33 % on the Standard QR `NotDetected` path. The shape test, centre run first, costs +9 to +21 %. For rMQR the table first sat after the scale and perspective searches and lost renders whose attempt budget those searches had spent. It now goes first. A single-module bound of 1.6 module sizes counted a three-pixel alignment run as one module on R11x27 (width 25, no such version). 1.2 separates them. The corner assertions led to putting the table first in Standard QR: 11 builder renders decoded through the fitted grids with a corner 0.85-1.3 px out.

Measured against the branch before this change, with 300 renders per cell at 1.0-1.25 / 1.25-1.5 px/module, nearest-neighbour renders at a random sub-pixel offset went Standard QR 41 → 300 / 96 → 300, Micro QR 85 → 300 / 127 → 300, rMQR 92 → 300 / 126 → 300, and builder renders went Standard QR 141 → 300 / 196 → 300, Micro QR 32 → 300 / 189 → 300, rMQR 58 → 300 / 135 → 300. 1.5-2.0 is unchanged at 300 (Standard QR crisp 299 both ways: one render at 1.97 px/module, past the 1.75 gate). Anti-aliased renders at the same densities move a little and are not the target: Standard QR 5 → 10 / 156 → 165, Micro QR 24 → 28 / 243 → 247, rMQR 103 → 119 / 260 → 270. Anti-aliased, bilinear and builder-shape renders at 1.5-3.5 px/module are identical except +1 and +2 in two Standard QR cells. Supersampled renders at 2-6 px/module, any rotation, a third keystoned, 3,000 per symbology, are identical render for render. On 18 two-level noise images the candidate counts are identical.

Lessons. When the margin goes to zero, stop estimating and read: every earlier repair in this series improved a measurement (a better module size, a fitted frame), and at (pitch − 1) / 2 no measurement is good enough, while the edges are exact and were in the image all along. An exact validation can replace a statistical one without widening what gets in: 49 modules through measured edges admit less than three ratios do, so no noise image gained a candidate. A bound borrowed from a neighbouring routine carries that routine's assumptions (1.6 module sizes was sized for fitted lines, where a long run is an error, not a different kind of run). Corner assertions belong in the first test of any new decode path. Here they were added late and changed the design.

Benchmark delta: within noise against the branch before this change at 10 iterations, with the two small symbols run three times interleaved: `M4_ImageDecode_Span` 7.39 / 7.49 → 7.54 / 7.57 µs, `R7x43_ImageDecode_Span` 7.99 / 7.78 → 7.90 / 7.98 µs, `Image_Byte_Url_V6_M_Decode (Span)` 33.26 → 33.32 µs, `R17x139_ImageDecode_Span` 39.62 → 41.23 µs, `NoSymbol_Noise_1144x168` 7,841 → 8,157 µs, `NoSymbol_Gradient_1144x168` 184.4 → 182.6 µs. On the failure paths (fastest of seven at 512 px), Standard QR `NotDetected` on 1 px two-level noise went 5.22 → 5.81 ms at 50 % density and 1.98 → 2.15 ms at 30 %, 2 px noise +4 to +8 %, and Micro QR and rMQR stayed within 2 %. Damaged Standard QR at 1.2-1.5 px/module (v10 at 100 px, v25 at 170 px, v40 at 250 and 370 px) went +2 to +25 % (156 → 178-202 µs on the smallest, 2.05 → 2.08-2.18 ms on the largest), because the table is one more sampling and decode. A damaged symbol this small that used to go undetected is now found and fails in its data, which costs what finding it costs (Standard QR v10 at 80 px 28 → 215 µs).

### F18 is closed, and what is left is measured against other readers (2026-09-21)

Done, with no code. F18 is closed with (a) to (d) shipped and (e) to (g) measured and not taken up, and the remaining accuracy work moves to a plan of its own, targeting the renders another reader decodes and this library does not (completed 2026-09-28 and folded into the three decoder records and the [image decode sweep](../specs/qrcode-test-fixtures.md#image-decode-sweep)).

(e) was measured and is not worth its own change. The sweep covered all 32 rMQR versions at any rotation with keystone on both axes and 3 % anisotropy, 1,200 renders per density band (1.6-2.9 / 3-6 / 6-10 px/module), with a column that samples through the true homography: every shipped failure reads that way, so all of it is frame estimation. At up to 4 % keystone the shipped decoder reads 1,188 / 1,200 / 1,200, and a row-scale search inside the perspective search adds 5. At up to 10 % it reads 1,127 / 1,157 / 1,143, and the search adds 13 / 0 / 0 while making a damaged warped symbol 2.2 to 2.9× slower to fail (20.5 → 59.6 ms). The failures lie elsewhere: width 139 is 16 % of them against 1-5 % for every other width, and they climb with keystone past 6 %. That is the perspective search's resolution over a long symbol, and the new plan carries it as an absolute rate. (f) and (g) stay as the review left them, reads bought with failure-path time at the two ends of the density range, with the numbers in the row.

F18 was closed instead of gaining an (h). A sweep of every encoder the repository can run (this library, ZXing.Net, QRCoder, QrCodeGenerator, CodeGlyphX, libzint and qrtool, in 23 render kinds and 135,000 decodes with no misread) checked that F13-F18 improved the decoder and not only the tests' own symbols. They did: per kind the read rate differs between encoders by at most 1.5 points, and every library's own image writer reads 100 %. The same sweep read each image with zxing-cpp and ZXing.Net, which is the better yardstick: it has an end, changing a test cannot move it, and it shows where the decoder is behind (Standard QR: bilinear upscales at 1.5-2 px/module, anti-aliased edges at 1.25-2 and keystone past 6 %, with 1,870 Standard QR renders zxing-cpp reads and this library does not), not merely where it is imperfect. Micro QR and rMQR are far ahead of zxing-cpp in every kind and are tracked by absolute rate there. The full table is the new plan's baseline.

Lessons. A list of failing classes found by one's own renders grows by a letter per sweep and never closes. A gap to another reader can close. The encoders were the cheap half of the question: whether foreign symbols read could have been asked at F13 with the oracles already pinned in `tools/`, and every sweep since would have carried the answer. Two tool facts cost the sweep its first runs: libzint's creator sometimes dies with an access violation on some payloads (first misread as a threading fault, and the [fixtures spec](../specs/qrcode-test-fixtures.md#lessons-learned) has the correction), and qrtool 0.13.2 writes a wrong R17x43 at level M (about 88 modules off this library's and libzint's matrices, which agree byte for byte).

Benchmark delta: none, because nothing under `src/` changed.

### Phase 5, Structured Append (2026-09-15 to 2026-09-29)

Done. It shipped in #409. On the decode side, `QRStructuredAppend` (`Index` 0-based, `Count`, `Parity`, `IsEmpty`) and `QRCodeDecodeInfo.StructuredAppend` are reported by every entry point that returns a `QRCodeDecodeInfo`. The header is read wherever it sits. A position past the count, a second header and a truncated header are `InvalidBitstream`. On the encode side, `QRCodeGenerator.CreateStructuredAppend(text, ecc, options)` splits text across the fewest symbols the `options.Version` cap allows, balanced so all share one version, and returns `Create`'s symbol when one symbol holds the text. The charset is decided once for the whole text and declared in every symbol, and the parity is the XOR of the whole text's bytes in that charset. For interop, the decode corpus holds 95 symbols in 14 sets from two pinned encoder lineages plus 4 third-party captures. Sets this library writes read back through three pinned readers (196 of 196 symbols) and match the pinned balancing encoder's parity on all 21 comparable combinations. Fourteen performance rounds cut the planning overhead of a 45,000-character, sixteen-symbol set from 83x (`Single`) and 1,240x (`Optimal`) of encoding its symbols alone to about 1.2x and 8.2x.
